articles.title: Marc Roca: "Ojalá Rodri no estuviera lesionado"
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista del Betis compareció ante los medios de comunicación
articles.summary: El centrocampista del Betis compareció ante los medios de comunicación
articles.body: Marc Roca, centrocampista del Betis convocado por primera vez con la selección española absoluta a los 29 años, lamentó este martes la lesión de Rodri Hernández, cuya ausencia le ha abierto las puertas del equipo de Luis de la Fuente, siete años después de disputar el Europeo sub-21 de 2019, al que tampoco acudió el actual futbolista del Barcelona por problemas físicos. "Al final siempre es una ilusión enorme estar aquí. Da igual si es de una forma u otra. Ojalá Rodri no estuviera lesionado. Me toca estar aquí, vengo con mucha ilusión y con ganas de ayudar al equipo. Vengo trabajando muy fuerte mucho tiempo y creo que he demostrado que tengo nivel para estar aquí", declaró en rueda de prensa. El destino ha vuelto a cruzar los caminos de ambos centrocampistas. En 2019, Rodri renunció a disputar el Europeo sub-21 porque consideraba que no se encontraba en las mejores condiciones físicas para afrontar el torneo. Marc Roca, que ya formaba parte de los planes de De la Fuente, disputó aquella competición y se proclamó campeón de Europa junto a futbolistas como Dani Olmo, Mikel Oyarzabal o Fabián Ruiz, ahora habituales en la absoluta. Siete años después, una lesión del jugador del Barcelona ha propiciado su primera convocatoria con España, donde se ha reencontrado con antiguos compañeros que durante este tiempo se han consolidado en el equipo nacional. "Cuando me vino la llamada pensé en los compañeros con los que me iba a reencontrar. Ha pasado mucho tiempo. Las personas siguen su camino, pero me han acogido súper bien. Me siento como en casa", explicó. También reconoció que su estreno internacional tiene un significado especial después de recorrer un camino mucho más largo de lo que imaginaba cuando conquistó aquel Europeo. "Mi camino ha sido muy largo, con momentos mejores y peores. Siempre lo he tenido como objetivo, siempre ha estado marcado en mi cabeza y en la de mi pequeño círculo. A mí me ha tocado esperar durante mucho tiempo", afirmó. En ese recorrido, que le llevó del Espanyol al Bayern de Múnich, después al Leeds inglés y finalmente al Betis, destacó la importancia de Manuel Pellegrini y de una operación de tobillo a la que se sometió hace año y medio para solucionar unas molestias que condicionaban su rendimiento. "Es una de las mejores decisiones que tomé en mi vida. Mi vida cambió a nivel personal porque arrastraba mucho dolor y también a nivel futbolístico. Estoy otra vez en mi mejor nivel", aseguró. Además, agradeció la confianza de Pellegrini, que le ha permitido recuperar su mejor versión, y reivindicó la constancia como una de las claves de su llegada a la absoluta. "No recuerdo la última vez que falté a un entrenamiento. Son muchos años de trabajo en la sombra, de constancia, de tener esa fe y ganas de querer ir siempre a más", manifestó. También dedicó palabras de elogio a De la Fuente, al que conoce desde las categorías inferiores y del que destacó especialmente su calidad humana. "Lo conozco de la sub-19 y en la sub-21 me tocó jugar el Europeo bajo sus órdenes. Sabemos de la calidad humana que tiene antes de lo futbolístico. Al final pienso que lo más importante es la persona y Luis siempre ha sido una persona excelente. Siempre lo ha demostrado. A nivel futbolístico es obvio todo lo que ha logrado. Mejor imposible. Ha ganado todo lo que ha jugado y ojalá siga durante muchos años ganando todo lo que se le ponga por delante", señaló. "Estoy muy contento por él. Si me dices cuando era sub-21 si me espero que Luis ganara el Mundial, pues queda un poco lejos, pero siempre le vimos con mucha capacidad, talento y calor humano que hace que el equipo rinda al máximo nivel como está demostrando. Ha sido un recorrido bueno y satisfactorio para él y ojalá que sea mucho más grande", añadió. Asimismo, destacó además la humildad de sus compañeros y eligió a Fermín López como el futbolista que más le ha impresionado durante sus primeros días en la concentración: "He tenido muchos referentes durante mi carrera. Busquets, Xabi Alonso, Rodri, Zubimendi... El centro del campo de España es el mejor del mundo. Es un orgullo estar aquí y representar a mi país y más con este centro del campo. Todos tienen muchísima calidad. Y aparte de la calidad. el grupo humano y las personas que hay detrás del jugador. Si me tengo que quedar con uno, es con Fermín", destacó. Por último, preguntado por si cree que España debería retirarse del Mundial si la final se disputa en otro país, dijo estar centrado en cosas más inmediatas: "Son cosas que no hay que preguntármelas a mí. Veremos qué pasa. Queda mucho tiempo. Ahora mismo tenemos retos más importantes que son los partidos de República Cehca e Inglaterra. Después pasará tiempo y ojalá se juegue en España. Sería lo mejor para todos. Pero falta mucho tiempo", finalizó

articles.title: Pellegrini pide "seriedad" y "ambición" para arrancar en la Copa del Rey
articles.standfirst: El técnico pone el foco en el debut frente al Navalcarnero y no piensa en el derbi del día 21
articles.summary: El técnico pone el foco en el debut frente al Navalcarnero y no piensa en el derbi del día 21
articles.body: El técnico del Betis, Manuel Pellegrini, atendió a los medios en la sala de prensa de la ciudad deportiva para valorar el choque del próximo jueves ante el Navalcarnero en la Copa del Rey. "Con mucha ilusión, ambición, de empezar con el pie derecho. Otra forma de entrar en europa y la final se juega aquí en La Cartuja", comenzó. "Con muchas bajas, pero hay un plantel que debe dar la cara en las tres competiciones. Lo importante es entrar con la seriedad que el fútbol exige. Hay ejemplos de equipos de menos nivel que eliminaron a otros de Primera. Al que le toque jugar debe demostrar por qué está en el primer plantel del Betis. Se cambió aquí porque estimamos que era más conveniente, había que cambiar otros partidos, teníamos Champions...". Antony. "Lo veo con la frustración de no estar en su mejor momento futbolístico, pero les pasa a todos. Es importante que mantenga la concentración y la intensidad necesarias. Tiene la calidad, tendrá partidos más adelante y entrenamientos para retomar su nivel y ojalá sea lo antes posible". Valles y la Selección. "Muy contento por ambos. Es un gran mérito llegar a la selección de tu país y poder enfrentarte a rivales importantes. Álvaro se ha ido recuperando todo el tiempo que estuvo parado el año antes de venir al Betis. Me alegro por él, le gusta trabajar y eso fue producto de su mejoría. Lo de Marc Roca indica la madurez que tiene como jugador". Giovani Lo Celso. "No hay ningún tipo de problema, hay 25 jugadores y mi labor es elegir a los jugadores que vi mejor durante la semana. Cada partido es distinto y pensé que había otros en mejor momento y sólo pasa eso. Hay un partido nuevo, veremos mañana los citados y el once inicial. No ha pasado nada con él, estimé que otros habían entrenado mejor y no pasa de ahí". Morante. "Yo creo que todos pueden tener más tiempo en el equipo. Uno evalúa como técnico cada día lo que cada uno hace, a veces la prensa no lo ve todo. Morante es uno más y creo que va por el camino correcto en la manera que lo estamos llevando". Navalcarnero. “Es un partido también con nosotros mismos. El rendimiento debe ir acorde a una seriedad. Siempre es una evalución para los jugadores. A veces uno hace rotaciones con jugadores que han jugado poco, pero en este caso casi todos han tenido bastante participación. Los que jugarán mañana han tenido participación en la Champions y en LaLiga. Entre todos hay que comenzar esta tercera competición con la ambición que hay que tener". Dani Ceballos. "Estuvo mucho tiempo sin entrenar y sin jugar. Todos conocemos la calidad que tiene. El otro día fue un ejemplo de cómo entrar motivado y exigido desde el banquillo. No pienso en el derbi para nada, primero terminamos la Copa del Rey el jueves, y después a sábado hay nueve días y veremos cómo llegan los jugadores. Sabemos la trascendencia emocional de un derbi y luego llega un partido de Champions en el que estamos obligados a ganar para buscar la clasificación". Renovación. "No es el tema en este momento. Estoy pendiente de la Copa, hay dos partes y se tienen que juntar, veremos lo que se estima conveniente". Cucho. "Comenzó ya a correr en el césped, hace solo trabajo de recuperación. Veremos cómo se desarrolla en la próxima semana para ver cuánto avanza, si no siente molestias". Récord de puntos. "Son todas estadísticas que son importantes llevarlas y reflejan algo, pero lo más importante es centrarnos en el futuro y queda muchísimo en las tres competiciones que estamos. Las cosas se demuestran en el terreno de juego y ojalá mantengamos esta regularidad. LaLiga es la que va a marcar el año, la Champions trae emocionalmente muchas cosas, pero esa estadística es porque no hemos dejado LaLiga atrás. Hemos tenido regularidad en las dos competiciones y eso lo hacen los equipos grandes".

articles.title: El Pucela 82-83: última esperanza del Málaga
articles.summary: Último recuerdo de permanencia milagrosa
articles.body: El Málaga CF ha entrado en una dinámica que empieza a adquirir tintes históricos. La derrota frente al Racing de Santander en La Rosaleda ha agravado todavía más la crisis de resultados de un equipo que, después de doce jornadas, continúa sin saber lo que es ganar en Liga. Los hombres de Juanfran Funes apenas han sumado cinco puntos de los 36 que se han puesto en juego, con un balance de cinco empates y siete derrotas. Unos números que le sitúan como colista y que convierten este comienzo de campeonato en el más negativo de toda su trayectoria en Primera División. Ni siquiera el recuerdo de la última aventura malaguista en la élite ofrece un escenario tan desfavorable. En el curso 2017-18, con Míchel al frente del equipo, el Málaga había alcanzado los siete puntos tras las doce primeras jornadas. Además, ya conocía la victoria, después de imponerse al Celta de Vigo por 2-1 en la décima fecha. Aquella temporada acabó con un descenso doloroso y el conjunto blanquiazul en la última posición, con 20 puntos. Ahora, el equipo presenta unos registros todavía peores que los de aquella campaña. La dimensión del problema también se entiende al repasar los precedentes de la máxima categoría. El Málaga se ha convertido en el decimocuarto equipo que encadena sus doce primeros partidos de una temporada en Primera sin conseguir un triunfo. De los trece conjuntos que vivieron anteriormente una situación similar, únicamente uno logró salvarse. Es decir, el 92,9 % acabó descendiendo. El Sporting de Gijón de la temporada 1997-98, con un solo punto en ese primer tramo, o la Real Sociedad de 2006-07 son algunos de los ejemplos de equipos que no consiguieron revertir una situación que terminó llevándoles a Segunda. El Córdoba de 2014-15 tampoco pudo escapar de ese desenlace. La estadística deja una única puerta abierta a la esperanza: el Real Valladolid de la campaña 1982-83. Los pucelanos llegaron a la jornada 12 con exactamente el mismo balance que presenta ahora el Málaga: cinco empates y siete derrotas. El cambio de rumbo comenzó desde el banquillo. Felipe Mesones fue destituido tras las diez primeras jornadas y, después de un encuentro con Santiago Llorente como interino, José Luis García Traid asumió el cargo el 12 de noviembre de 1982. La primera victoria todavía tardaría en llegar. Fue el 5 de diciembre, en la jornada 14, con un 2-0 precisamente ante el Racing de Santander. Aquel equipo consiguió reaccionar y terminó el campeonato en la duodécima plaza, aunque en una Liga de 18 participantes en la que la permanencia se alcanzó con 25 puntos. El Valladolid terminó con 29. Ese precedente es ahora el principal argumento al que puede agarrarse el malaguismo para no dar por perdida la batalla. La otra referencia está mucho más cerca en el tiempo: la remontada protagonizada por el propio Juanfran Funes la pasada temporada en Segunda División, cuando tomó un equipo en puestos de descenso y acabó conduciéndolo hasta el ascenso. El técnico necesita encontrar una fórmula parecida para cambiar el rumbo de un Málaga que está contra las cuerdas. La historia demuestra que existe una excepción, pero también deja claro que el camino hacia la permanencia se presenta extraordinariamente complicado.

articles.title: Jesús Vázquez sufre una lesión en el aductor derecho y estará entre tres y cuatro semanas de baja
articles.standfirst: El lateral izquierdo sufre una lesión muscular sufrida en los minutos finales del partido ante el Real Madrid
articles.summary: El lateral izquierdo sufre una lesión muscular sufrida en los minutos finales del partido ante el Real Madrid
articles.body: Jesús Vázquez estará entre tres y cuatro semanas de baja después de que las pruebas médicas realizadas por el Valencia hayan confirmado que sufre una lesión en la musculatura del aductor de la pierna derecha, producida durante el encuentro del pasado sábado ante el Real Madrid en Mestalla. El club, como suele ser habitual, no ha detallado un plazo de recuperación, aunque este tipo de dolencias suele requerir alrededor de un mes de recuperación, por lo que el lateral izquierdo podría reaparecer a finales de noviembre o principios de diciembre. En el escenario más optimista llegaría a tiempo para el encuentro ante Osasuna; en uno más conservador, su regreso se produciría frente al Getafe. La lesión obligó al defensor valenciano a caerse de la convocatoria para el encuentro de Copa del Rey que el Valencia disputa este martes ante el Tavernes y que habría sido un buen momento para sumar minutos ya que perdió protagonismo precisamente con la llegada del técnico mexicano. Su ausencia reduce las opciones de Javier Aguirre en una demarcación en la que el técnico había encontrado en el futbolista valenciano una solución recurrente para dosificar minutos teniendo en cuenta que está apostando de manera recurrente por José Luis Gayá para el once titular. Para Aguirre, le lesión de Vázquez supone un contratiempo teniendo en cuenta que Gayá fue expulsado en el partido de Liga contra el Real Madrid lo que le llevará a perderse el siguiente encuentro de la competición ante el Rayo. Por otra parte, el hecho de que esta baja se haya producido antes de un parón de Liga, permite al lateral valenciano pasar parte del período de recuperación en un momento en el que hay menos competición en Liga.

articles.title: Luis García tiene la enfermería llena
articles.standfirst: El Mallorca se entrena con diez bajas a cuatro días de recibir al Córdoba
articles.summary: El Mallorca se entrena con diez bajas a cuatro días de recibir al Córdoba
articles.body: Luis García tendrá que hacer un equipo competitivo mientras esquiva las numerosas bajas que tiene en su plantel este fin de semana. Las seguras son los cuatro internacionales: Valjent, Luvumbo, Bergström y Guille Fernández, convocados con sus respectivos países durante el parón internacional. Por su parte, Morlanes y Roca siguen recuperándose de sus respectivas lesiones, ambas de larga duración. Además, hay algunos futbolistas que son duda para el choque ante el Córdoba y que no se han ejercitado hoy junto a sus compañeros. John Chetauya ni siquiera ha saltado al césped y se ha ejercitado en el gimnasio. Por su parte, Josep Cerdà, David López y Jan Salas han realizado trabajo específico y siguen recuperándose de sus molestias musculares. Las cuentas son claras para recibir al Córdoba este sábado en Son Moix: seis bajas seguras y cuatro piezas en duda para completar un puzle en el que el técnico asturiano tendrá que tirar de futbolistas del filial. La nota positiva en Son Bibiloni la ha protagonizado Dani Luna, que, tras meses en el dique seco, se ha ejercitado junto a sus compañeros.

articles.title: El Eibar impone su autoridad en Mutilva
articles.standfirst: Los armeros vencieron con comodidad al CD Pamplona gracias a un doblete de Magunazelaia y otro tanto de Martón
articles.summary: Los armeros vencieron con comodidad al CD Pamplona gracias a un doblete de Magunazelaia y otro tanto de Martón
articles.body: El Eibar no dio lugar a la sorpresa en su visita a Mutilva y avanza ala segunda eliminatoria de la Copa del Rey. Los hombres de Jokin Aranbarri vencieron con comodidad al CD Pamplona. Lo mejor para evitar sorpresas es arrancar con fuerza y eso es lo que hizo el cuadro armero, que a los dos minutos ya mandaba en el marcador gracias a un gol de Martón. Magunazelaia, con un doblete, puso más tierra de por medio y apagó cualquier esperanza del conjunto navarro. Aranbarri dio minutos a canteranos como Llorente y Ortuzar, pero por encima de la presencia de los dos jugadores del filial, destacó el regreso a la competición de Olaetxea y Sergio Álvarez después de superar sus lesiones.

articles.title: El Leganés, sufriendo más de lo esperado, se clasifica bajo la lluvia
articles.standfirst: Un gol de Álex Millán al inicio de la segunda mitad permite a los pepineros superar a un combativo Trival Valderas
articles.summary: Un gol de Álex Millán al inicio de la segunda mitad permite a los pepineros superar a un combativo Trival Valderas
articles.body: El Leganés encontró un pequeño respiro en la Copa del Rey después de superar por la mínima al Trival Valderas en Butarque. Los de Luis Carrión, necesitados de una alegría tras sus últimos tropiezos ligueros, cumplieron con el objetivo de avanzar de ronda, aunque sin ofrecer una imagen especialmente convincente ante un rival de categoría inferior, milita en Tercera RFEF, que plantó cara durante buena parte del partido. Carrión aprovechó la eliminatoria para introducir novedades y dar protagonismo a jugadores menos habituales. Sin embargo, al conjunto pepinero le costó encontrar espacios y transformar su superioridad en ocasiones claras. El Trival, bien organizado y con mucha ilusión, consiguió mantener el empate sin goles hasta el descanso. Nada más comenzar la segunda mitad llegó el tanto decisivo. Álex Millán aprovechó una asistencia de Naim para adelantar al Leganés en el minuto 48 y encarrilar la clasificación. Con el marcador a favor, Carrión movió el banquillo y dio entrada, entre otros, a Marvel, Atienza y Álvaro Morata. El Trival no bajó los brazos y siguió compitiendo hasta el final, pero el Leganés consiguió conservar su ventaja. Una victoria necesaria para recuperar algo de confianza y seguir vivo en la Copa, aunque el equipo pepinero continúa obligado a mejorar sus prestaciones para cambiar su preocupante dinámica en Liga. FICHA TÉCNICA.- Trival Valderas: Aitor Arias; Cristian Guzmán (Samuel Alale, 58’), Adrián Jiménez, Raúl Díez, Benedict Adom; Ivi, (David Rodríguez, 58’), Marcos Gozalo, Daniel Pascual, Godfred Yeboah (Y. Bayano, 78’), Francisco Reguera (Víctor Calarge, 78’); y Álvaro Rivero (Tanke, 17’). Entrenador: Raúl Montero. Leganés: Raúl Fernández; Naim (Suleiman, 71’), Javi Montero, Pulido, Jorge Martínez; Dani Rodríguez (Marvel, 63’), Zico, Kechta (Morata, 81’), Soko (Álex Sancrís, 71’); Unax del Cura (Atienza, 63’) y Álex Millán. Entrenador: Luis Carrión. Gol: 0-1. 48’ Álex Millán, tras asistencia de Naim. Árbitro: Abraham Domínguez Cervantes (Colegio Andaluz). Amonestó a los locales Ivi, Tanke y Raúl Díez y a los visitantes Javi Montero y Naim. Estadio: Ontime Butarque. 2.093 espectadores.

articles.title: Roig refuerza a Iñigo: "Hemos apostado por un proyecto muy bueno y confío en que los resultados lleguen"
articles.standfirst: El presidente amarillo reconoce que están pasando por un momento difícil
articles.summary: El presidente amarillo reconoce que están pasando por un momento difícil
articles.body: La victoria del pasado fin de semana ante el Getafe fue liberadora para el Villarreal. Los amarillos llegaban de su semana más difícil tras la dura derrota ante el Espanyol y la goleada ante el PSG. Pese a ello el presidente Fernando Roig se muestra convencido de la apuesta a largo plazo realizada por el técnico, Iñigo Perez: “Todos estamos animados, con ganas , y por eso llevamos 27 años en primera y 18 en Europa. Hemos apostado por un proyecto muy bueno y espero y confío que los resultados sean buenos” El mandatario valenciano afirmó que el último partido no era una examen en exclusiva para el técnico navarro, toda vez que reconoció que están pasando por un momento complicado: “No era un reválida para Iñigo, sino para todo el equipo. Llegaremos a un buen sitio y los que ahora pitan luego aplaudirán y dirán que no han pitado en la vida. En los momentos difíciles, y ahora lo es, es cuando hay que apoyar” De la misma forma hizo referencia a la cifra de 1000 partidos en Primera que firmó su equipo este pasado fin de semana y la efusiva celebración que protagonizó en el palco tras la reciente victoria ante el Getafe: “Mil partidos son muchos, es una gran satisfacción y más poder celebrarlo con una victoria tan importante . Tras la semana que hemos pasado era para estar muy contentos. Hay que animar a todo el equipo. Ya tenemos 15 puntos que nos acercan al primer objetivo que es salvar la categoría. Luego ya llegará lo demás”, comentó También se refirió a la importancia de los próximos partidos de Liga de Campeones que su equipo disputará tras el parón ante Slavia de Praga y Sabah, en los que seguramente se jueguen la clasificación: “ En la Champions hay que sacar los máximos puntos posibles. De momento ya tenemos el triple de puntos que la temporada pasada, pero ahora tenemos que conseguir todos los que podamos”

articles.title: Gol: passageira com deficiência será indenizada em R$ 10 mil em MG | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão do TJMG manteve condenação da Gol por danos morais a passageira de Formiga e determinou a devolução em dobro do valor pago pela cliente.
articles.summary: A Gol Linhas Aéreas deverá pagar R$ 10 mil de indenização a uma passageira com deficiência que teve o desconto de 80% para seu acompanhante negado pela companhia.
articles.body:
Gol nega desconto em passagem e é condenada a indenizar passageira com deficiência em MG — Foto: Christyam de Lima/Divulgação

A Gol Linhas Aéreas deverá pagar R$ 10 mil por danos morais a uma passageira com deficiência após negar o desconto de 80% na passagem do acompanhante dela . A decisão foi mantida pela 13ª Câmara Cível do Tribunal de Justiça de Minas Gerais (TJMG), em julgamento de um recurso relacionado a um caso ocorrido em Formiga , no Centro-Oeste do estado.

Além da indenização, a companhia aérea também deverá devolver em dobro o valor cobrado pela passagem do acompanhante, totalizando R$ 3.157,26.

A passageira precisou recorrer à Justiça depois de solicitar o benefício tarifário, previsto para acompanhantes de pessoas com deficiência que necessitam de assistência durante o voo.

Segundo o processo, ela enviou os formulários e laudos médicos exigidos pela empresa, mas não recebeu o desconto. Com isso, precisou pagar R$ 1.578,63 pelo bilhete do acompanhante.

Na ação, a cliente apontou falha na prestação do serviço, violação ao dever de informação e falta de prioridade durante o desembarque.

A Gol alegou que a concessão do desconto dependia de avaliação técnica e que os documentos médicos apresentados estavam incompletos, além de terem sido enviados em prazo insuficiente para análise. A empresa também atribuiu à passageira a responsabilidade pelo ocorrido.

Ao analisar os recursos apresentados pelas duas partes, a relatora, desembargadora Maria Luíza Santana Assunção, negou tanto o pedido da companhia aérea para anular ou reduzir a condenação quanto o da passageira, que queria aumentar a indenização para R$ 20 mil.

Segundo a magistrada, ficou comprovado que a documentação médica foi enviada dentro do prazo regulamentar estabelecido pela Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (Anac).

A relatora considerou que a ausência de resposta da companhia configurou falha na prestação do serviço e violação ao dever de informação. Ela também destacou que a recusa do benefício prejudicou uma passageira em situação de vulnerabilidade e atingiu sua dignidade.

Os desembargadores Ivone Guilarducci e José de Carvalho Barbosa acompanharam o voto da relatora.

O g1 entrou em contato com a Gol Linhas Aéreas, que informou que não irá comentar a decisão.

articles.summary: El '10' del Oporto acumula siete goles y cinco asistencias en lo que va de curso
articles.body: No tiene el 'foco' de las cinco grandes Ligas, pero la de Gabri Veiga (O Porriño, 2002) es, seguramente, por rendimiento, una de las grandes ausencias en la lista de Luis de la Fuente. El 'cerebro' del Oporto está tirando la puerta abajo en este inicio de curso. "No le falta nada para llegar a la selección. Es cuestión de 'timing' y de la calidad que hay en la selección. España, al igual que Portugal, es una de las mejores selecciones del mundo. Tienen mucha calidad en el centro del campo. Desde mi punto de vista, pero tiene todas las características para estar ahí", aseguraba Francesco Farioli tras conocer que el ex del Celta se había quedado fuera de la convocatoria para los partidos de la Nations League contra Inglaterra y República Checa. "Mi trabajo es entrenar al Oporto y gestionarlo mientras esté aquí. Y lo está haciendo de maravilla. Creo que su progreso es muy evidente. Está mejorando en regularidad y en su capacidad para recuperar energías cada tres días. Estamos muy satisfechos con su evolución; trabaja duro para mejorar", insiste el entrenador de los 'dragones'. Lo cierto es que los números de Gabri Veiga, elegido 'MVP' de la Liga portuguesa en agosto, no dejan de 'engordar'. El '10' es el 'Pichichi' del Oporto: suma siete goles, cinco en Liga, entre todas las competiciones. Acumula, además, cinco asistencias. Dicho de otra forma: ha participado en el 34,28% de los tantos que han marcado los 'dragones', que marchan líderes con cinco puntos de ventaja sobre el Benfica después de haber ganado las 11 jornadas que se han disputado hasta la fecha. Sólo Gianluca Prestianni (4) ha sido elegido más veces 'MVP' que el ex de Al Ahli en lo que va de Liga (3). Por si fuera poco, Gabri Veiga es el segundo jugador que más grandes ocasiones de gol genera (6) en Portugal, el cuarto que más centros efectúa (58) y el séptimo que más disparos a portería registra (10). "Nada de lo que ha hecho sorprende; era imposible que alguien con sus características se quedara en Vigo. Maduró aún más, se formó en Arabia Saudí y ahora está de nuevo en la élite del fútbol europeo en Portugal. Conoce su papel en cada momento del partido y no tiene límites. Seguirá brillando en el Oporto y estará en la selección española. Llegará muy lejos", confesaba Vladimir Gudelj, delegado del Celta, en declaraciones recogidas por 'O Jogo'. Venía de coronarse campeón de Asia con Al Ahli en 2025, pero en la goleada sobre el Nápoles (4-1) se consagró en Europa. Asistió a Jan Bednarek en el 1-0 y marcó el 2-1 en el 71'. Recibió al hueco de Santi Giménez y batió, mano a mano, a Alex Meret. Un nuevo recital que le valió otro 'MVP'. "Estoy en un buen momento, con confianza y energía", reconocía Gabri Veiga, visiblemente 'tocado': "He estado muy enfermo. Llevo dos días con antibióticos. Han sido unos días muy díficiles, tanto física como psicológicamente, por el accidente ferroviario que ocurrió en España y el fallecimiento de Jesús de Miguel. Fue una tragedia que me afectó mucho. Por suerte, pude dedicarle el gol. Descanse en paz". Veiga, internacional sub 21 en 19 ocasiones con Luis de la Fuente, evitaba, sin embargo, referirse a una hipotética llamada de España: "Eso no depende de mí. Estoy en un país donde tengo a los mejores del mundo por delante. Soy jugador del Oporto y, si llega el momento, llegará, pero mi atención está puesta en el Vitória Guimaraes." En Do Dragao, mientras tanto, siguen disfrutando de su mejor versión. “Ha mejorado físicamente, ha vuelto con un nivel de confianza diferente, ha crecido y se ha vuelto más maduro. La calidad siempre ha estado ahí, pero ha dado un paso adelante físicamente. Es un líder y se está convirtiendo en un jugador cuya actitud en el campo puede influir en el equipo. Cuando juega a este nivel todo parece más fácil y mejor", subraya Farioli. El 'dragón' Veiga está 'on fire'.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino: Man Utd open talks over replacing Michael Carrick.
articles.summary: Manchester United open talks with Mauricio Pochettino about replacing Michael Carrick, who is expected to lose his job.
articles.body:
Manchester United have opened talks with USA head coach Mauricio Pochettino about replacing Michael Carrick, who is expected to lose his job this week.

Carrick's future at United will be decided at a meeting in Monaco on Wednesday that will be attended by chief executive Omar Berrada, director of football Jason Wilcox and co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

And discussions for former Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino to return to the Premier League are under way.

United have spoken to the ex-Argentina defender about their managerial position on three previous occasions - when Jose Mourinho was sacked in 2018, then in 2022 before the club appointed Erik ten Hag and again when the Dutchman was sacked in 2024.

Pochettino renewed his contract with the USA in August, and they have a two-legged Concacaf Nations League quarter-final against Haiti over the next week.

The 54-year-old has a $10m (£7.5m) release clause.

Berrada and Wilcox have flown to Monaco for one of their regular, planned meetings to discuss strategy around the football club.

On this occasion, the main issue to be decided is Carrick's future and what should happen next.

It is expected that Berrada and Wilcox's recommendation is for the head coach to go.

Carrick was pictured arriving at the club's Carrington training base on Wednesday.

United are 18th in the Premier League - inside the relegation zone - after winning just one of their first 10 games and none since August.

It is the club's lowest position at this stage of a top-flight season since 1986-87, when they were 20th.

Pochettino's first job in the Premier League was at Southampton from January 2013, before a five-year stint at Tottenham from 2014 that included a Champions League final appearance.

He managed Paris St-Germain from January 2021 to July 2022 before spending the 2023-24 season in charge of Chelsea.

Pochettino moved into international football by taking the USA job in September 2024, and led the co-hosts to the last 16 of the 2026 World Cup.

articles.body: La grave crisis que vive el Manchester United le ha obligado a tener que plantearse muy seriamente un cambio de aires en el banquillo. Su amplia experiencia en la Premier League, tras sus pasos previos por el Tottenham y el Chelsea, lo convierten en una opción sumamente atractiva para los de Manchester. El obstáculo contractual y la cláusula con la selección estadounidense sería el único inconveniente, ya que el entrenador firmó recientemente una extensión de contrato por cuatro años con la selección de fútbol de los Estados Unidos. articles.title: Bruno Guimaraes won’t be in the Arsenal team when they play Newcastle United at St James’ Park
articles.summary: Back on Saturday 8 August 2026, Bruno Guimaraes left St James’ Park, left Newcastle United, as he signed for Arsenal. Throughout the summer transfer window i...
articles.body:
Back on Saturday 8 August 2026, Bruno Guimaraes left St James' Park, left Newcastle United, as he signed for Arsenal.

Throughout the summer transfer window it had become clear that the Gunners were doing everything they could to get the Brazil international on the cheap.

Arsenal attempting to take advantage of the fact that Bruno Guimaraes was willing to leave, Mikel Arteta and the North London club trying to sign United's best and most important player for £50m or less and shamelessly using media stooges to try and force Newcastle's hand.

One thing we had learned with the sales of players such as Alexander Isak (£125m), Sandro Tonali (£100m) and Anthony Gordon (£70m), was that these Newcastle United owners were never going to allow any player leave for less than the club's valuation.

In the event, Arsenal eventually accepted that they had to belatedly act in a professional manner, made an official approach and Newcastle United reluctantly accepted £75m for a player who next Monday (16 November) will turn 29.

Nobody at Newcastle United , whether the owners, players, manager, fans, would have chosen to sell at even that price. It was only because Bruno Guimaraes wanted out and the club reluctantly allowed him to leave.

Now in ten days time Bruno Guimaraes will make his first return to St James' Park.

A 5.30pm kick-off as Newcastle United host Arsenal.

There is zero chance of Bruno Guimaraes being named in that Arsenal team to take on Newcastle United.

He won't want to play and Mikel Arteta won't want to select him.

Arteta has made clear that Bruno Guimaraes is only a squad player at Arsenal, the former Newcastle United captain now used as back up to the likes of Declan Rice and defender turned midfielder Myles Lewis-Skelly. The Brazil international with only four Premier League starts in his first three months at the club.

Bruno Guimaraes has always been somebody who lives on the edge when it comes to his emotions, one of the reasons why Newcastle United fans loved him so much. However, with this match he would be a walking liability for Arsenal, a fragile character in danger of at any time letting his emotions getting the better of him on his return to St James' Park.

If we needed any further proof of his fragile state, back in October, fully four weeks before the St James' Park return, Bruno Guimaraes made clear that it was already preying on his mind.

Almost three months after leaving Tyneside, he Arsenal player for 'some' reason decided to revisit the moment he left Newcastle United.

Bruno Guimaraes releasing a statement declaring it was "one of the toughest decisions of my life"…

The Arsenal player stating: "It was very difficult for me because I had an amazing relationship with everyone at Newcastle United…I did my best for the club. I was there for almost five years and inside of me, I just wanted a new challenge. To be fair, it was very tough for me to make this decision because I really enjoyed my time at the club, the affection I had for the fans. It was a difficult one. I lost many, many nights of sleep because it was difficult for me, for my family…I think I did great for Newcastle. We won a trophy after 70 years. We got into the Champions League twice. We got to two finals. I think I did what I could for the club. I wish them all the best because they were so nice to me. It is just time to move on. I have been enjoying my time here at Arsenal as well."

Why come out with that them? It was almost as though Arsenal are due to visit St James' Park and that fact is now in the forefront of Bruno Guimaraes' mind…

Bruno Guimaraes going on to say: *"It was not just hard to tell Eddie [Howe], but to tell the owners, my team-mates. But I think the club went to a new rotation, a lot of players left as well. The gaffer left as well. It was tough, because my connection with the club was unbelievable. I never felt so loved like the way I was at Newcastle. I hope I can have the same love here at Arsenal, but the connection I had was unbelievable. It was hard for me to say bye to them. I remember, when I said bye to the lads, I was crying. They were crying as well, because we were a family there."*

Bruno Guimaraes needs to put his violin away. Nobody put a gun to his head, he chose to leave St James' Park.

Personally, I don't have a problem with him deciding to leave after more than four and a half years at St James' Park. Almost all players decide to leave one or more clubs at some point and/or the clubs decide that themselves. You can't have it both ways though.

Eddie Howe, the Newcastle United players and fans, were special to Bruno Guimaraes, just not special enough. Bruno Guimaraes simply showed us that he was not really any different to any other player, making a decision for his own benefit at the expense of the club that he says was so special to him. He made the decision, nobody else, so now he has to accept the consequences when he visits St James' Park.

I won't be giving Bruno Guimaraes any abuse on Saturday 21 November but I won't be clapping him either. He chose to play for another club and their fans, he is no longer anything special at Newcastle United. He was when he was here but that was the past.

As I said earlier, absolutely zero chance that Bruno Guimaraes will start the game on 21 November.

The only chance the Newcastle United fans will get the chance to show their 'appreciation' for their former captain will be during the warm-up. Unless say Arsenal go a couple of goals up, then I could maybe see the possibility of Bruno Guimaraes coming on as a late sub.

The excuse for his omission from the Arsenal team that faces Newcastle United, will no doubt be the fact that he is currently away with Brazil. They play Japan on Saturday 14 November and then play Singapore the day after Bruno turns 29 on Tuesday 17 November, in Singapore. The travelling etc will be blamed for his omission from the Arsenal team that plays at St James' Park.

It will be a strange experience seeing Bruno Guimaraes back at St James' Park.

Somebody who was such a key and inspirational figure for Newcastle United, first name on the team sheet, now sitting on the opposition bench and desperate not to be asked to step onto the pitch.

articles.title: Bringing the heat works just fine with Notre Dame's star linebacker
articles.summary: KVA’s takedown of a Heisman Trophy candidate for that 11-yard loss marked the first sack by a Notre Dame football linebacker this season.
articles.body:
SOUTH BEND — When Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa sacked Miami quarterback Darian Mensah on the opening defensive series of the second half, Notre Dame Stadium shook with delight.

"It was electric," the junior linebacker said after practice on Tuesday evening Nov. 10. "We'd been practicing that pressure all week, so when it hit in the game, it was like all that work paid off. It was awesome."

Current Irish linebackers entered Saturday's game with 19.5 career sacks among them. Jaylen Sneed led the way with 6.5, followed by Drayk Bowen (4.5), Viliamu-Asa (4.0), Jaiden Ausberry (2.5) and Madden Faraimo (2.0).

KVA's takedown of a Heisman Trophy candidate for that 11-yard loss marked the first sack by a Notre Dame linebacker this season. It also marked the 13th straight game the Irish defense got off the field without surrendering points on its first series after halftime.

Notre Dame football hosts Miami in primetime | Top photos

With Bowen on crutches after right ankle surgery, Notre Dame defensive coordinator Chris Ash had no choice but to give Viliamu-Asa a career-high 70 defensive snaps (out of a possible 76).

His previous high was 62 in a 2025 win over Boise State. That was the only other time he reached 50 snaps while sharing time in an uber-talented linebacker room.

After missing the season opener against Wisconsin as he worked back from a second torn ACL, the former St. John Bosco star maxed out at 35 defensive snaps in the loss at BYU. That night, he aggravated a wrist/thumb injury he'd suffered initially at North Carolina on Oct. 3.

Held out of the Stanford and Navy games while he tried to heal, Viliamu-Asa didn't just step in for Bowen at middle linebacker. He inherited the "green dot" helmet, enabling sideline communication from defensive coordinator Chris Ash.

"There were definitely a couple times where I couldn't hear coach, so I had to look at the sideline for the signal," Viliamu-Asa said. "It was a great environment Saturday night."

'Smelling blood' against Miami's Darian Mensah

Notre Dame's pass rush also got on a roll against an 80% passer in Mensah. At times, that required sending five- and six-man pressures at a Hurricanes offensive line that had struggled at times in pass protection (tied for 82nd nationally with Wisconsin, per Pro Football Focus).

"We tried to bring pressure," Notre Dame coach Marcus Freeman said Monday. "We brought an extra guy on quite a few pressures, and we knew we couldn't let Mensah get comfortable. He is an elite quarterback, and he was even more impressive in person. His ability to elude pressure and not take a sack, his ability to manage the game and put the ball in really good places. He earned my respect.

"But we didn't want him to be comfortable. We wanted to speed him up. We wanted to speed up his decision-making process."

The result was 32 total pressures against Mensah, who went 24-of-43 passing (56%) for 276 yards, three touchdowns and one interception. Nine of those pressures were from Irish linebackers: four by Viliamu-Asa, three by Sneed and two by Ausberry.

"It was fun to get after him," Viliamu-Asa said. "When you get quarterbacks off their platform and get them anxious like that in the pocket — talk about smelling blood."

And while Notre Dame has frequently asked its linebackers to drop into zone coverage during Ash's 21-game tenure, Irish linebackers who played for predecessor Al Golden from 2022-24 know the cumulative benefits of bringing the house.

Might a night like Saturday against the Hurricanes inspire Ash to sic his linebackers on opposing quarterbacks more often?

"Shoot, I hope he liked it, yeah," Viliamu-Asa said.

A steady diet of man-to-man coverage seemed to work against Miami sans Malachi Toney. Why wouldn't it click against the three remaining teams on Notre Dame's November menu: Boston College, Southern Methodist and Syracuse?

"Shoot, I'm cool with it," KVA said. "Whatever (Ash) calls, I'm going to play."

Mike Berardino covers Notre Dame football for the South Bend Tribune and NDInsider.com. Follow him on social media @MikeBerardino.

articles.title: Joan Garcia reveals Barcelona’s approach to Mourinho and Real Madrid tensions: ‘We need to distance ourselves’
articles.summary: Barcelona goalkeeper Joan Garcia says winning the Champions League is a major objective in 2026/27, but insists it must not become an obsession. In an interv...
articles.body:
Barcelona goalkeeper Joan Garcia says winning the Champions League is a major objective in 2026/27, but insists it must not become an obsession.

In an interview with Mundo Deportivo , he discussed his development under Hansi Flick and urged Barcelona to ignore the noise surrounding Real Madrid and Jose Mourinho.

Champions League ambition must not become an obsession

When asked whether the expectations surrounding the Champions League create additional pressure, Garcia made it clear that Barcelona are targeting every available trophy.

"Obviously, it's a target for us, just like the League, the Cup and the Super Cup. I think we've got the squad to compete and try to win all the competitions, whilst recognising just how difficult that is.

"I can see the team is very motivated. It's a target, but it doesn't have to become an obsession, because that can end up being counterproductive.

"It remains an ambitious and demanding target, and we're looking forward to taking it on," he analysed.

Joan Garcia says Barcelona should not feel the pressure of winning the Champions League. (Photo by Eric Alonso/Getty Images)

Simply put, Garcia wants Barcelona to pursue every trophy without allowing the pressure surrounding Europe to become counterproductive.

Garcia says Barcelona are still gaining experience

The goalkeeper also reflected on his development since joining Barcelona , explaining how adapting to Flick's playing philosophy has helped him understand his responsibilities better.

"Well. I think that, little by little, the team and I are improving and gaining experience.

"We're learning to handle different situations that we perhaps didn't know how to manage before. I think that's positive and will serve us well for the future.

"I'm still adapting to the style of play and the various areas where we need to improve.

"Little by little, I'm starting to feel more comfortable, and I'm gaining a clearer understanding of what I can contribute, what I can't, and when to act and when not to.

Garcia says Barcelona should avoid the noise concerning Real Madrid. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

"I think that's all part of the learning process – of continuing to grow and learn. I'm keen to carry on," he noted.

Joan Garcia urges Barcelona to ignore Mourinho noise

Asked how Barcelona should respond if tensions with Real Madrid increase under Mourinho, Garcia said the squad must concentrate on its own performances.

"I think we need to distance ourselves a little more from all that and focus on ourselves.

"We're clear that, if we're doing well and getting things right, everything else – whatever people do or say out there – doesn't affect us," explained the international goalkeeper from the Spanish national team's training camp.

"it would be a mistake to focus too much on that, especially within the dressing room.

"Obviously, it's different outside, but in the dressing room I don't think we need to pay it so much attention," he concluded.

articles.title: Pellegrino, el '9' más 'cabezón' de Europa sigue esperando a Argentina y España: "No cierro ninguna puerta"
articles.standfirst: Es, junto a Budimir, el jugador que más goles marca de cabeza en las grandes Ligas
articles.summary: Es, junto a Budimir, el jugador que más goles marca de cabeza en las grandes Ligas
articles.body: Mateo Pellegrino (Valencia, 2001) continúa haciéndose un nombre en el 'calcio'. El ex del Parma, fichado este verano por la Fiorentina a cambio de 22,5 millones de euros, 'abrió la lata' en el empate contra la Juventus (2-2). Lo hizo con un gol 'marca de la casa' que le valió el 'MVP'. El hijo de Mauricio Pellegrino -pasó por la cantera del Valencia- cabeceó a la red un córner botado por Pedro Gonçalves para poner el 1-0 en el 4' y lo celebró 'a lo Batistuta', disparando con la 'metralleta'. "Vi un vídeo suyo y lo imité... pero aún me falta mucho para ser como él", reconocía a 'DAZN'. En el Artemio Franchi ha caído de pie. Suma ya cinco goles, cuatro en Serie A y uno en 'Coppa', en 12 partidos. "Esperaba un mejor comienzo como equipo, pero personalmente estoy contento con cómo he empezado la temporada con la Fiorentina", admite. Lo realmente llamativo de Pellegrino Jr. es su portentoso juego aéreo. "Desde que marcara su primer gol de cabeza en Serie A (8 de marzo de 2025, ningún futbolista de las grandes Ligas ha marcado más tantos con este recurso. Suma nueve, igual que Ante Budimir", apunta 'Opta'. "El remate de cabeza es uno de mis puntos fuertes. Lo trabajamos mucho durante la semana. Queremos marcar más goles a balón parado", confiesa el hispano-argentino, que evita, sin embargo, marcarse cifras: "Un gol siempre es un gol. Me gusta marcar de cualquier forma, pero no me pongo una cifra. No me gusta, prefiero ir partido a partido. Me gustaría marcar tantos goles como sea posible". El dorsal 32 de la Fiorentina, internacional sub 19 con Argentina, sigue esperando una llamada. Lionel Scaloni le incluyó en la prelista para el Mundial... pero se cayó y no ha llegado a debutar, por lo que podría, también, jugar con España. "Si tengo la opción de las dos y me ofrecen lo mismo, elijo Argentina. Yo me siento argentino. Quiero un montón a España, nací ahí, tengo amigos y pasé muchos años de mi vida , pero me considero argentino", reconocía a 'El Equipo de Deportea' allá por 2024. Un discurso que 'matizó' a principios de año en 'ESPN' después de que se le empezara a especular con una posible llamada de Luis de la Fuente: "Es lindo que se hable de la posibilidad, pero no me dijeron absolutamente nada. No cierro ninguna puerta, nunca. A nivel de clubes, de selección tampoco... Me enfoco en lo que tengo que hacer y después, el día de mañana, veré si tengo que tomar una decisión". El nuevo 'killer' de la Fiorentina comenzó su carrera a imagen y semejanza de su padre: jugando de defensa. Fue, precisamente, el exjugador de Valencia, Barcelona y Alavés quien le invitó a 'mudarse' de área. "Me enseña cómo comportarme bajo presión, qué hacer para no darle vueltas a ciertas situaciones y me da consejos. Hablamos a menudo en casa. Fue mi primer entrenador, pero sigue siendo la persona que más me motiva", confiesa Mateo. Mauricio, internacional con Argentina en tres ocasiones, disfruta de los goles de su hijo en la distancia: actualmente dirige a Lanús. "Mateo está creciendo. Está en un lugar en el que está siendo feliz y ama jugar a la pelota. Al principio le costó mucho, tuvo lesiones, jugó poco y Platense le abrió las puertas para que demuestre su fútbol. Ahora en Italia, está compitiendo, sumando minutos y metiendo goles", subraya. Ahora cuenta con la ayuda del madridista Mastantuono. "Creemos en él. Franco es un chico especial e increíblemente humilde. Tiene muchas ganas de aprender, es bueno de cara al gol y posee una técnica excelente. Esperamos que pueda rendir muy bien con nosotros", asegura Mateo Pellegrino mientras sigue esperando una llamada.

articles.title: Andoni Iraola was sacked from his first job at AEK Larnaca in Cyprus: Liverpool manager’s difficult career start explained
articles.summary: Andoni Iraola is now in charge at Liverpool and at the top of his game but his journey in management began in Cyprus with AEK Larnaca and ended in the sack. Adam Bate finds out what went wrong and whether his subsequent rise could have been predicted…
articles.body:
Iraola learned from the experience and rebuilt his career back in Spain with Mirandes before really impressing with Rayo Vallecano and Bournemouth to earn his opportunity at Anfield. Nevertheless, it must be curious for his old colleagues to witness the rise.

Were there any believers that day in January when Larnaca drew 2-2 at home to Ermis Aradippou, the team that would go on to finish bottom of the table? It extended the run of league games without a win to six and Iraola paid the price for that streak with his job.

Were there clues beyond the results that Iraola was destined for bigger things and merely the victim of a trigger-happy firing culture at the Cypriot club? Speaking to David Catala, who played under him at Larnaca, including in that final game, he did see promising signs.

"He already had very clear ideas of what he wanted," Catala tells Sky Sports . "You saw it and, for sure, all the players were speaking about how he was going to become a fantastic coach. But to reach this level? To say that he would be at Liverpool? That is a big claim."

Iraola had spent his entire playing career in Europe at Athletic Club prior to a brief sojourn stateside with New York City. His first foray into the managerial game with Larnaca put him outside of his comfort zone, even if there was a Spanish constituency in the club.

His initial impact was impressive. Three rounds of qualifying for the Europa League group stage were successfully negotiated with wins over Dundalk, Sturm Graz and Trencin. Just as significantly, the players at Larnaca readily embraced Iraola's illuminating ideas.

"To be in the Europa League for a club in Cyprus was amazing," explains Catala. "And the work that he did was good. These were the same ideas that he wants at Liverpool, actually, pressing high and wanting to be very aggressive with and without the ball."

In Cyprus at that time, this was particularly rare. "The rhythm of the game there was very slow. I was able to play there until I was 38 years old because that rhythm was not so high." Iraola had a different vision of the game, learned under Marcelo Bielsa in Bilbao.

Catala explains: "Everything was more explosive with him, more rhythm, more intensity. You saw how Marcelo did it with Athletic Club. I remember sometimes it was like that for us. Crazy things like following man-to-man all over the pitch. That was crazy as players."

He recognises now that it was a taste of the future of the game. "Football has gone in that direction. The way you have to press. It changed the mentality of the players." Even the game in that country. "He changed a little bit the rhythm of the league in Cyprus."

For a while, it worked. At the start of December, 10 games in, Larnaca were second in the table to Limassol, the only team to beat them during that period. Iraola's side were actually ahead of the six-time reigning champions and the eventual title winners APOEL.

But it all unravelled quickly. There was a 5-1 home defeat to Bayer Leverkusen in Europe that was sandwiched between a trio of away trips on the island that yielded no wins. A home defeat by the odd goal increased the pressure before the brief Christmas break.

A loss away to Omonia followed by that draw against strugglers Ermis sealed his fate. There were some formation tweaks but nothing major. "He did not change too much in terms of his thinking about the way of playing against different teams," recalls Catala.

The real lesson was that even in an environment that was supposed to be away from the spotlight for such a high-profile figure during his playing days, pressure comes quickly in football. "If you are not getting results, it is difficult to have the trust of the owners."

Catala explains: "Cyprus is very difficult for coaches, and especially for young coaches, because the owners of the football clubs, they are very passionate. And at the moment that you are not getting the results, they sack the coach like they are just peanuts.

"As soon as you lose games, especially against the lower teams, immediately the fans are speaking with the owner and the owner is going crazy. You cannot have the stability that maybe you need when you are a young coach. This is what happened to Andoni."

For Catala, who would go on to manage Larnaca himself, lasting a little longer than Iraola, he has tried to take things from his old coach. And believes Iraola too will have benefited from that experience. "It was still a good choice to start there," he insists.

"Cyprus is not an easy place for anyone to work but it is a good place for a young coach to start their journey. He had the opportunity to coach a team in the Europa League, for example. Unfortunately, football everywhere is now very unstable for all coaches.

"It was a short period. But he would have learned many things from his experience in Cyprus about how to manage situations. It was his first job, you have to take something from that. For sure, he has improved a lot since then and he has developed himself."

Into the Liverpool coach, no less. "I am happy for him. If you look at the last years, you can see that he is obviously a fantastic coach. I cannot say that I did not expect it, but it is a little bit of a surprise." From the sack at Larnaca to Liverpool, how could it not be?

articles.title: Jordan Hadaway interview: Meet the 25-year-old Llandudno boss - the youngest top-flight manager in Europe
articles.summary: Jordan Hadaway has been in charge of Llandudno since August 2023; at 18, he was managing Caerwys and a 41-year-old captain; now 25, he has a UEFA A Licence and took the Seasiders back to the Cymru Premier with promotion in 2025/26
articles.body:
Once almost exclusively the preserve of former professionals, a playing career is no longer a prerequisite.

That has opened the door to the younger generation. Thirteen managers and head coaches in England's top four divisions are under 40, with Brighton's Fabian Hurzeler the youngest at 33.

But the Cymru Premier - formerly known as the Welsh Premier League - is home to the youngest top-flight manager in Europe.

Last season, Jordan Hadaway guided Llandudno to promotion from the Cymru North. In July, he turned the grand old age of 25.

A thirst for knowledge and a willingness to do the hard yards

Hadaway already had the presence of mind to focus on coaching, rather than playing, by 14.

He completed his Level 1 Leaders Award two days after his 16th birthday and was working towards his UEFA B Licence by 18, when he was in charge at Caerwys and working with a 41-year-old captain.

Later, he coached for the Real Madrid Foundation and, in 2024, he passed his A Licence. He counts Nigel Adkins and Robert Earnshaw among those to have helped him along the way.

During his time at Caerwys, Hadaway wrote to Roy Hodgson, who was then in charge of Crystal Palace.

"He was the oldest manager in league football and I was the youngest manager in football, so my college tutor said to me 'Why don't you just write to him?'" he tells Sky Sports .

"I got an email from his personal assistant and he invited me in, but the day I was due to go down, Covid happened. By the time everything opened back up, he had been sacked!

"It was a bit of a nightmare because I really wanted to go and meet him, but I guess things happen for a reason, don't they?"

It is clear his strong work ethic has helped him progress.

"While I was studying at Liverpool Hope University, some days I'd be up at 2.30am or 3am going to work in the bakery for a family friend as they'd lost staff because of Covid," he says.

"I'd stay there until 9.30am, go to a lecture from 11am until 2pm and then I'd coach from maybe 4pm until 9pm. It was a full-on period in my life!"

And it has not slowed down, given he now balances his part-time managerial role with a full-time role as a teacher.

In December 2022, Hadaway left his role as assistant manager at Cefn Druids to become Llandudno U19s manager, as well as the club's head of youth development.

By the start of the 2023/24 season, he had been named interim first-team manager of a club whos squad and staff had been decimated after its artificial playing surface was condemned by the Welsh FA.

"Everyone had walked away and we were two weeks away from starting the season," he recalls.

"The chairman said to me: 'Will you just try and keep us in the league and make sure we have a club? I don't care if we get relegated if that's what has to happen as long as we've got a team and a club at the end of it.'

"Everyone around me, I'll be honest, told me don't take it. My mum even says to me today: 'I can't believe you took that job'.

"But I saw it as an opportunity to go and try and prove people wrong at a very big club in Wales that has an amazing facility and a good fanbase.

"I had the smallest budget in the league by a country mile. I had one player two weeks before the start of the season and no management team. I had to put all that together in two weeks. We were favourites to get relegated, but I never once thought we would.

"We managed to finish 12th out of 16 and we got to a cup final that year. It's quite incredible, really."

Two years later, he took the club one step further.

"My aim was always to be a Welsh Premier League manager by the time I was 27, 28. Did I ever think I was going to get there? No. It's amazing.

"I'm lucky I've had very good players and very good staff that have enabled me to push the club to that standard. It's not all about me, it's about everybody involved.

"I got quite emotional on that afternoon we got promoted. It was an achievement that probably will stick with me and be one of my best forever."

Asked if he has aged beyond his years with the way his career has progressed, Hadaway quips: "Yes - I think my hairline's shown that!

"A lot of people say I'm the oldest 25-year-old they've ever met. I think I am mature, but I'm mature because of the people I've grown up around. The people you spend the most time with have the biggest impact on you."

That maturity is reflected in his attitude towards what comes next.

Many would leap to the conclusion that, if he is doing well at 25 in Wales, a career over the border in England will be on the cards soon.

That may well come to be true, but Hadaway is in no immediate rush.

"Don't get me wrong, I would love to do it [work in the Premier League or EFL]," he adds.

"However, I love my job and I love supporting young people that need the support in school, and I think it would have to be a very good opportunity to take me away from what I'm doing currently. I'm also not naive.

"But I don't think I should get given a chance because I'm the youngest manager in top-flight football - I think I should be given a chance because I'm good enough.

"If we had this interview again in 10 years' time and I was still at Llandudno, I would be happy, because I'm not someone that chases the stars. I'm someone that likes to make sure I'm doing a good job where I'm at and make sure that when I leave, I've left it in a very good place and it's stable."

For someone who has accomplished so much so young, perhaps Hadaway's strength is in knowing there is no need to rush.

articles.title: Liverpool incorrectly denied penalty for Jurrien Timber pull on Alexander Isak vs Arsenal, rules independent panel
articles.summary: Alexander Isak was not awarded a penalty during Arsenal's win at Liverpool in November despite Jurrien Timber pulling his shirt; referee Andy Madley gave nothing on-field and VAR Stuart Attwell did not intervene; independent Key Match Incidents (KMI) panel gives verdict
articles.body:
The Key Match Incidents (KMI) panel assesses refereeing incidents across every Premier League match and voted 4:1 that referee Andy Madley should have awarded Liverpool a spot kick.

The panel also voted 3:2 that VAR Stuart Attwell should have intervened and sent Madley to the pitchside monitor on the basis that it was a clear and obvious error.

Arsenal led 1-0 through Kai Havertz's goal, which proved to be the winner, when Isak attempted to head Bradley Barcola's cross in the 21st minute on November 1, but was pulled back by defender Timber.

One KMI panellist believed "the short-lived holding to lack clear impact on the ability of Isak to progress", while two panellists argued, "the subjectivity in assessing impact meant this did not meet the high threshold for VAR intervention".

Isak stayed on his feet during the incident and Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola said afterwards he would tell the striker to go down next time.

So far this season 196 KMIs have been examined, with the correct on-field decision taken in 86 per cent of cases. That rises to 97 per cent following VAR intervention.

Jamie Carragher: "One of the best goalscorers in the league is pulled back seven yards out and it stops him heading the ball - why does he need to make a meal of it? VAR, do your job."

Ian Wright: "He shouldn't have to make more of it. We can see it... Unless I'm pulled back, I'm going to head it as much as I can. When he pulled him, it was just about enough as he would need to go down.

"VAR is wrong in this instance. If they gave that penalty, I wouldn't sit here and say 'I can't believe they gave that'."

Gary Neville: "It's actually unnatural not to make more of it. When you get pulled and you're just about to score, you ordinarily complain like crazy. It's a very odd reaction from Isak."

Daniel Sturridge: "Unfortunately, he (Isak) has not fallen over. You're supposed to fall over, put your arms in the air and show the referee you're mad about it... to me, his reaction is almost like 'VAR, do your job'.

"But they've not done their job. He shouldn't have to make more of it - clearly, he shouldn't. Everyone can see that his arm is stretched, he [Timber] is holding him with a stretched-out arm."

Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher: "It depends which angle you watch it from. The first angle, you see nothing. That is the referee's angle.

"The second angle, which is what VAR looks at, and it is a lot more damning.

"VAR looks at it in slow motion, which is another thing against him. In normal speed, he grabs and grabs him quickly but let's go. Does he do enough [for a penalty]?

"What is Timber's intention? He is on the wrong side of him. Does he do enough to stop him? He [Isak] will say yes, as he is close to the ball.

"VAR would be accused of re-refereeing if it is a penalty. It is a case of damned if they do and damned if they don't.

"It has to be the case of on-field. The more I watch it, the more I think he [Timber] has taken a big chance and has got lucky."

What happens if Isak goes down? "Once a player hits the ground, there are more questions to ask.

"There is asking what has knocked him down. Has he gone down by his own momentum, has he slipped or has he been pulled or pushed?

"Once you factor that in, obviously you have a different decision. He [referee] has to deal with the situation he has seen. He has seen a little pull of the jersey and thought no penalty."

Jay Bothroyd: "Where was the referee? Every angle, I can see it is a penalty.

"He has pulled his shirt. How can none of them [referee and VAR] see that and say it is a penalty? I can't comprehend that. I don't get it.

"That is one of the most obvious penalties [I have seen]. He is running forward! He has stifled his momentum going forward, to stop him heading the ball.

"Every angle I look at, even normal time, I said it could be a penalty. I look at it now, the more I see it, the more I ask myself how they have missed it! How do they lose focus and not get that."

Andoni Iraola: "The Isak one is a clear penalty. We can all see that he holds the t-shirt. The ball just goes one centimetre in front of Alex. Alex is going to hit the ball in front of the goal."

On whether the player needed to go down: "The fact that you are even asking me that shows he should have gone to the floor. If he does, they call the penalty 100 per cent.

Asked whether he will tell Alex to go down next time: "Yes, definitely."

Virgil van Dijk: "I've seen it back and I've seen it given as well on other occasions. Today it wasn't meant to be.

"The VAR doesn't notice it? There are 50 cameras. Even more. Why does he have to complain when there are so many cameras? It is spotted because everyone's seen it.

"In the end, it wasn't given and we lose the game unfortunately, so well done to Arsenal."

From Arsenal's perspective, Mikel Arteta said he had not watched the incident back and had no comment when asked by Sky Sports.

Mac Allister reaction 'clearly exaggerated'

Towards the end of the second half, Liverpool midfielder Alexis Mac Allister went down holding his face after his forehead touched with Noni Madueke's .

VAR reviewed the incident, and the Arsenal winger was not sent off. Instead, Mac Allister was booked.

The KMI panel unanimously felt the referee was correct not to show Madueke a red card as the contact was "negligible" and Mac Allister's reaction "clearly exaggerated".

Referee and VAR missed Ipswich penalty vs Hull

The KMI panel also ruled that Ipswich Town should have been awarded a penalty in their 2-2 draw with Hull City on October 3.

Nobel Mendy was judged to have committed a holding offence against Dara O'Shea during a corner in the 18th minute, with the score still goalless.

The panel voted 4-1 that referee Tom Kirk should have awarded a penalty, while VAR Neil Davies should also have recommended an on-field review.

The majority agreed there was "a clear sustained holding offence", although one panellist felt O'Shea and Florentino Luis's actions during the incident should have been considered, meaning a penalty was not warranted.

articles.title: Mbappé no se entrena con Francia
articles.standfirst: El galo se ha quedado trabajando con los médicos y fisioterapeutas
articles.summary: El galo se ha quedado trabajando con los médicos y fisioterapeutas
articles.body: El delantero galo del Real Madrid no se ha ejercitado este miércoles junto al resto de sus compañeros y ha permanecido trabajando con los médicos y fisioterapeutas de la federación. Desde la Federación Francesa de Fútbol han querido rebajar cualquier preocupación y aseguran que la ausencia del atacante del entrenamiento grupal no se debe a una lesión, aunque el capitán de los 'bleus' ha seguido un plan individualizado de trabajo. La situación está siendo seguida de cerca desde Valdebebas. Fuentes del Real Madrid consultadas por MARCA transmiten tranquilidad y recuerdan que "Mbappé se controla muy bien" a nivel físico, por lo que la gestión de las cargas durante los periodos internacionales forma parte de la normalidad. La selección dirigida por Zinedine Zidane afronta además una ventana exigente, con dos compromisos de máxima exigencia ante Italia y Turquía que obligan a gestionar cuidadosamente el estado físico de sus principales estrellas. Francia se juega buena parte de sus objetivos internacionales y Mbappé sigue siendo la gran referencia ofensiva del combinado galo. La noticia llegada desde la concentración francesa coincide además con el regreso anticipado de Aurélien Tchouaméni al Real Madrid. El centrocampista abandona la concentración y volverá a la disciplina blanca, una circunstancia que permite al club recuperar efectivos antes de la reanudación de la temporada.

articles.title: Super League clubs vote to expand competition to 15 teams for 2027 season with London Broncos favourites for inclusion
articles.summary: Super League clubs have voted to expand competition to 15 teams for the 2027 season; Championship side London Broncos are favourites for inclusion; the league also voted in favour of two salary cap amendments that allow clubs more flexibility with young players and injuries
articles.body:
"Super League (Europe) Ltd has today held a shareholders' meeting to determine how many clubs will take part in the competition in 2027," a statement from the league read.

"Having agreed in favour of moving from 14 to 15 clubs, SLE has passed their decision on to the Rugby Football League Board.

"The RFL Board will now set out criteria and assemble a panel to run the process to judge against it.

"A recommendation will be made in due course."

It is understood that clubs will now be invited to apply to be the 15th team in the competition.

London Broncos, who have made no secret of their desire to be in the top flight, completed the treble in 2026 during a brilliant season for them in the Championship. They are expected to apply to be the next club in Super league. It is not yet known if any other clubs will join the process. After London went back down to the Championship, they were took over by an ownership group including NRL and Brisbane Broncos legend Darren Lockyer.

Super League clubs approve salary cap amendments

Clubs also voted in favour of two amendments to the league's salary cap regulations that allow clubs more flexibility with young players and injuries.

The first allows teams to claim salary cap dispensation if a player is injured for over eight cap-relevant matches, allowing clubs to sign a replacement player for the period.

It also forbids teams from claiming further salary cap dispensation should a player who was already exempt from salary cap implications becomes re-injured later in the season, unless he missed a further eight matches which affect the salary cap.

The second allows teams to feature a young player aged 23 and under - who has not previously played in any salary capped games - in two matches without triggering an increase in a club's salary cap spending, with that figure increasing to 50% should they play between three and five matches.

Should the player feature in more than five matches, the full amount of their salary will be applied to the cap.

articles.title: Man City: Are Enzo Maresca's side's issues psychological or tactical?
articles.summary: The ongoing international break gives manager Enzo Maresca much-needed time to fix the growing issues in his Man City squad.
articles.body:
The ongoing international break will give Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca much-needed time to fix the growing issues in his squad.

The Italian made a dream start after taking over from Pep Guardiola in the summer, leading the club to a record seven consecutive victories at the beginning of the Premier League season.

But three consecutive defeats have followed as they have fallen six points adrift of league leaders Arsenal , who are looking in imperious form as they aim to retain their title.

In September, it was announced that City had been found guilty of breaking the Premier League's financial rules, and matches have continued as the club await the outcome of their appeal.

With possible sanctions hanging over them, is City's recent league form down to psychological issues or are there tactical problems Maresca needs to address?

Maresca's dream start turns into nightmare as title hopes hit

Property, football and politics: The links between Manchester and Abu Dhabi explained

Renowned sports psychologist Dr Paul McCarthy has 25 years' experience working in the industry with top clubs in England, Scotland, Germany and France.

McCarthy works on the personal and professional lives of players and says both contribute to how well they perform on the pitch, with the need to "piece together a jigsaw" when situations become disrupted.

"Players are like everyone else - they talk about what is going on in their own lives and things that are topical, especially about uncertain events," McCarthy tells BBC Sport.

"It generates communication with a lot of stories and rumour and over time if there are enough losses, there often becomes a reduced collective efficacy.

"A collective efficacy is a squad's belief in their ability to do what they need to do [to win] and because of their success in the past, that is often shaken a little by consecutive losses."

'Uncertainty leads to a lack of perceived control'

City were sitting pretty at the top of the table after a flawless start, but have dropped to third - behind Arsenal and Brighton .

After the guilty verdict was announced during the last international break, Maresca's men won their first game back - against 10-man Liverpool at Anfield - then narrowly overcame Ipswich at Etihad Stadium in their following match.

But they have since lost to Aston Villa , Brighton and Nottingham Forest , with defensive issues exposed and individual mistakes proving costly.

In their first seven games of the season, City did not concede any goals because of individual errors - but that has shifted dramatically in the past three matches, with four mistakes from players contributing to goals.

City have conceded 13 goals after 10 league games - their highest total at this stage of a season since 2008-09, when they had let in 16 - and that has prompted questions about their defensive solidity.

Asked if the uncertainty over the ongoing appeal process may affect the focus and attention of players, McCarthy said: "Yeah, that would be a very reasonable human response.

"When people are uncertain about their future, that uncertainty leads to a lack of perceived control, so uncertainty is often more stressful than bad news and the research shows that.

"So while you are waiting and you don't know the outcome, you are uncertain of where you are and there is that lack of control for a lot of people - they come to training, they play their games and it's outside of their responsibility."

'Anderson can't single-handedly resolve build-up play'

While at Chelsea , in a video for NBC Sports, Maresca discussed his tactics - moving counters into a 3-2-2-3 shape before pushing one up to create the 3-1-6 shape.

He explained using six attackers was a tactic he had employed against Inter Milan to outnumber their back five.

This season, he has adopted the 3-1-6 shape more permanently - trading a second holding midfielder for an extra attacking midfielder.

Coaching a team full of quality footballers, there is logic to wanting to play in a more front-footed and imposing manner, but how well tactics are performed depend on the skillset of the players asked to do them.

The big questions come in the form of Elliot Anderson and his midfield partners.

Anderson - naturally more of a roaming midfielder - leans on his physical strengths. At Nottingham Forest , he defended intensely, pressed high and wide, and contributed to attacks. This season, Maresca and his staff have looked to mould him into more of a sitting midfielder after the departure of Rodri in the summer.

Learning that role will take time, as it did for Rodri when he first joined.

It is not problematic in its own right to try to coach a player into a key role, but City have looked exposed through the middle of the pitch more often in recent games.

Anderson, who has largely impressed, has played to his habit - stepping out of a holding midfield position to attempt to press or track opposition players, often looking to win the ball back. Clever opponents have used this to drag him out of position before finding players through the middle.

With City looking to press high and often in a man-to-man fashion, Anderson has had to cover more space with his partners in midfield lacking the physicality required to support him.

When City are in possession, Enzo Fernandez - often one of City's midfield three - makes frequent attacking runs off the ball into the final third. When this happens, City can find themselves with as few as two or three players behind the ball, giving opponents favourable conditions to counter-attack if they can break the initial press.

For Maresca, the issue is less around the shape, and more around losing the ball in the first instance. After the loss to Forest, he said: "You concede transitions when you lose the ball, and when you don't win duels."

Further concerns arise when assessing the skillset of the players behind Anderson.

Gianluigi Donnarumma is not a goalkeeper renowned for his ball-playing ability. The defensive cohort are serviceable on the ball but have made costly errors under pressure, playing out from the back, this season too.

Guardiola's solution to mitigate some of these issues last season came in the form of asking midfielders to shoulder more ball-playing responsibility.

The loss of Rodri and especially Bernardo Silva, who would drop deep and take City from their own goal into midfield alone, have made City's problems more obvious.

As good as Anderson is, he is not a player who can single-handedly resolve build-up play as Bernardo Silva did, but Ayyoub Bouaddi may be somebody that could be used in this manner as we saw him against Brazil's press in the World Cup.
