articles.title: Nusa se viste de Diomande: "Nuestra forma de jugar se parece bastante"
articles.standfirst: El extremo lidera al RB Leipzig tras la salida del madridista con seis goles y ocho asistencias
articles.summary: El extremo lidera al RB Leipzig tras la salida del madridista con seis goles y ocho asistencias
articles.body: Antonio Eromonsele Nordby Nusa (Oslo, 2005) era la gran apuesta de futuro del RB Leipzig. Dicho de otro modo: el Diomande antes de Diomande. Tan es así que el extremo del Real Madrid, más versátil, se vio 'desplazado' a la derecha para 'liberar' la banda izquierda en favor del internacional noruego. Aun así, Diomande, que registró 13 goles y 10 asistencias en 36 partidos, consiguió 'golear' a Nusa, que cerró el curso con apenas cinco dianas y cuatro pases de gol en 35 encuentros. “Él jugaba por una banda y yo, por la otra, y cuando tenía el balón, disfrutaba viéndolo. Nuestra forma de jugar se parece bastante. Tiene una habilidad extraordinaria. Fue muy bueno aprender de él e incorporar algunas cosas a mi juego”, reconocía Nusa en una entrevista con 'El País' antes de reencontrarse con Diomande en el Bernabéu. Ahora, ya sin el marfileño y con permiso de Brajan Gruda, vuelve a sentirse el líder de la 'manada'. "Con 14 ó 15 años, tenía más talento que Erling", aseguraba Gaute Larsen, que entrenó a Nusa y Haaland en el Bryne. "Me gusta generar caos", reconoce este regateador empedernido que creció admirando a Neymar: "Es mi modelo a seguir. Uno de los mejores del mundo". Más que caos... está sembrando terror. Estamos a principios de noviembre y el ex del Brujas, fichado en 2024 a cambio de 21 millones de euros, ya presenta los mejores guarismos de su carrera: acumula seis goles y ocho asistencias en los 15 partidos que ha disputado entre Bundesliga, Copa y Champions. Al Manchester City, sin ir más lejos, le volvió loco... a pesar de acabar perdiendo 2-3. En Bundesliga -está nominado a jugador del mes de octubre- está a un nivel superlativo: es el segundo máximo asistente (7) y el segundo jugador que más goles (11) ha producido. Su 'dribbling' causa estragos: es el cuarto jugador que más regates realiza en el último tercio del campo (20) y el quinto en total (37). Todo ello con el segundo mejor porcentaje de acierto (78,4%)... y transportando el esférico toda velocidad. Nusa es el cuarto jugador de la Liga alemana que más conducciones progresivas realiza (25) de la Liga alemana y el séptimo que más distancia (2.253 metros) recorre en 'sprint', a más de 25,2 km/h. “A cada uno le gusta una cosa de manera instintiva, y lo mío era el regate. Siempre he disfrutado el fútbol así. Es lo que soy. Tuve mucha suerte. Nunca encontré a nadie que me dijera que podía o no podía hacer algo en el campo. Cuando intento que mi mente interfiera en lo que mi cuerpo quiere hacer, no funciona. Me siento mejor cuando dejo que mande el cuerpo", insistía el extremo en 'El País'. El que verdaderamente lo disfruta, a pesar de los riesgos que asume en forma de pérdidas, es su entrenador, Martín Demichelis. "En mi opinión, es uno de los mejores extremos de Europa en este momento. Es difícil pararlo", asegura el extécnico del Mallorca. “Siempre he creído en mis cualidades”, asegura el extremo, que no dudó en hacer autocrítica tras la 'manita' que endosaron al Hamburgo (5-0): "Quizás no obtuve el rendimiento que merecía la temporada pasada, pero trabajo duro y sólo intento ayudar y marcar tantos goles como sea posible". El Diomande antes de Diomande vuelve a 'reinar' en Leipzig.

articles.title: USMNT's Mauricio Pochettino, Manchester United Reportedly Finalizing Contract amid Carrick Rumors
articles.summary: While Michael Carrick technically remains the manager at Manchester United, the club have already identified his successor.
articles.body:
While Michael Carrick technically remains the manager at Manchester United, the club have already identified his successor.

David Ornstein of The Athletic reported the club is finalizing a contract with United States men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino if the decision is made to part ways with Carrick.

Pablo Iglesias Maurer and Jamie Jackson of the Guardian reported Tuesday therewas mutual interest between the two sides.

Pochettino signed a new contract with U.S. Soccer this August, with the idea to keep him in the role through the 2030 World Cup. The Athletic's Paul Tenorio, Tom Bogert and Henry Bushnell reported the buyout "is in the ballpark of $10 million."

Jason Burt of the Telegraph reported that Pochettino "is in no rush to leave the U.S. team." However, he's hopeful of returning to club management at some point and has been intrigued in the past by the challenge of coaching Manchester United.

Having Pochettino leave three months after giving him an extension would be less than ideal for U.S. Soccer. Ripping the bandage off now might be better than the alternative, though.

Even if he stays, this is something that could hang over the national team over the next few years. If he decides to accept a club position at a later point, that's less time for a new coach to execute their plan for the World Cup.

Manchester United hiring Pochettino would carry risk for both sides.

The 54-year-old took Southampton to an eighth-place finish in the Premier League in 2013-14 before moving on to Tottenham Hotspur. Spurs were PL runners-up in 2016-17 and third in 2015-16 and 2017-18. They also reached the Champions League final in 2018-19, losing to Liverpool.

While at Tottenham, Pochettino excelled at player development and delivered an entertaining style on the pitch.

Pochettino's subsequent spells at Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea were far less memorable. His time with the U.S. national team is following along the same lines. A lot of the excitement surrounding the United States' performance in the group stage dissipated after a 4-1 hammering by Belgium in the round of 16.

Much like when it appointed José Mourinho in 2016, Manchester United might be getting Pochettino at a point when he's no longer a world-class manager.

From the coach's perspective, he'd be exchanging the relative stability of his current job for one of the most fraught in the sport.

For more than a decade after Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement, United has been mired in a cycle of dysfunction. It was too much to overcome for experienced managers such as Mourinho, Louis van Gaal and David Moyes along with Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim, who built their profiles outside of England.

Given how far removed he is from his Tottenham peak, an underwhelming tenure at Manchester United could make it difficult for Pochettino to parachute into another major club.

articles.title: El descanso eterno en el Spotify Camp Nou, más cerca
articles.standfirst: El proyecto del Memorial para los seguidores azulgranas está en marcha
articles.summary: El proyecto del Memorial para los seguidores azulgranas está en marcha
articles.body: Las obras de remodelación del Spotify Camp Nou abarcan muchos espacios, y uno de ellos es el Memorial que el club tiene proyectado construir próximamente, con columbarios y placas conmemorativas. El futuro Memorial, situado a pocos metros del terreno de juego del Spotify Camp Nou, ocupará una superficie de 1.500 m². El proyecto, que se abrirá a finales de 2027, ofrecerá dos modalidades de homenaje y recuerdo: depositar las cenizas de un ser querido en un columbario o inscribir un nombre y un mensaje en una placa conmemorativa. Ambas opciones estarán abiertas a barcelonistas de todo el mundo, sean o no socios de la entidad azulgrana. Muchas personas se han interesado en el proyecto, entre ellas, varios exjugadores y familiares de figuras históricas del Barça han manifestado su voluntad de formar parte de esta iniciativa. Tanto los columbarios como las placas conmemorativas podrán contratarse por periodos de 10, 25 o 50 años, con la posibilidad de elegir su ubicación dentro del Memorial. Los columbarios tendrán capacidad para una urna y mostrarán el nombre de la persona en el frontal. En todas las modalidades de columbario existirá la posibilidad de depositar posteriormente las cenizas en el ara comunitaria, una opción incluida en las concesiones de 50 años. La zona, que tendrá grandes murales dedicados a momentos destacados de la trayectoria del Barça además de elementos visuales, audiovisuales y sonoros, contará con un acceso permanente desde la calle.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino: Manchester United's approach for former Tottenham and Chelsea boss questioned
articles.summary: Sky Sports News’ Kaveh Solhekol questions Manchester United’s treatment of Michael Carrick, the influence of the Glazers and Ratcliffe, and whether the club’s latest managerial pursuit exposes deeper problems at Old Trafford
articles.body:
United have struck an agreement with the US National team to replace Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino , Solhekol believes Pochettino wouldn't be the top target for any other top clubs.

'Pochettino would not be up for one of the top jobs'

"I think he's a very good manager, but would he be in the frame to get the Liverpool job if that was available?

"Would he be in the frame to get the Arsenal job if that was available? Bayern Munich, Barcelona, Real Madrid, would they be looking at Mauricio Pochettino?

"This is somebody who I don't think got the Spurs job the last time it was available.

"I think short term, it would be a good appointment. The players will definitely respond to having somebody like Pochettino in charge and having him calling the shots. But long term, I hope Mauricio knows what he's letting himself in for if he does become the next United manager.

"Look, if you're looking for somebody with a proven track record in English football who's available, Eddie Howe's got a better CV. Howe's won a domestic trophy in English football, with Newcastle United. Antonio Conte has won the title in his first season at Chelsea.

"So there are people out there who have a better track record than Pochettino.

"Mauricio is a very good manager. He did a good job at Southampton. I think they finished eighth. He did a good job at Spurs. They came close to winning the title. They got to the Champions League final. But in five seasons at Spurs, he didn't win anything.

"He went to PSG. He had Neymar, Mbappe and Messi. I think he was appointed in January. They finished second. It's the only time in the last nine years that they haven't won the title. The following season, they did win the title. I think they won the French Cup under him as well. But he was sacked by PSG.

"He went to Chelsea, another very political club. How long did he last at Chelsea? He lasted one season. They finished sixth. They won their last five games of the season. Some of the fans wanted him to stay. I think one of the owners wanted him to stay. Another owner didn't want him to stay. He lasted one season.

"Then he went to the USA. And he's done a pretty good job. He hasn't set the world on fire. I've watched some of the USA games at the World Cup. They were the home nation. There was a feel-good factor around the side. But they were comprehensively outplayed by Belgium in the Round of 16.

"So if you look at his CV, you would say Mauricio Pochettino is a very, very good manager. But I think under normal circumstances, he would not now be getting one of the top jobs at the other biggest clubs in the world."

'They could have had him for nothing in the summer'

"Since Sir Alex Ferguson left Manchester United, if United were to fire Carrick and hire Mauricio Pochettino, they will have spent more than £100m hiring and firing managers.

"And if they get Mauricio Pochettino, everyone's reporting that they'll have to pay $10m to get him. Couldn't they have had him for nothing in the summer? In July, his contract with the USA ran out. He was available then.

"United by then, I think, had already appointed Michael Carrick. But surely they would have known that he was going to become available?

"I'm just intrigued to know who at Manchester United is really pushing for Pochettino to get the job."

'Why are you letting Carrick suffer in public?'

"I don't think this looks good for Manchester United at all. Most people in football will think this is a pretty shameful way to treat Michael Carrick, an incredible player for the club. Somebody who is Manchester United through and through.

"Why are you letting Michael Carrick suffer in public? What's the point of a chief executive and director of football flying to Monaco to rubber-stamp the sacking of Carrick when it is an open secret in football now that Carrick is leaving and he is going to be replaced by Pochettino?

"I know this was a pre-arranged meeting about more than just Carrick, but it's obvious this makes United look bad."

'Who's running the club? Who's making these decisions?'

"Well, who's running the club? Who's making these decisions? There's a chief executive (Omar Berrada), there's a director of football (Jason Wilcox).

"A lot of United fans don't want them to be at the club. They think the chief executive doesn't have enough experience as a chief executive, no experience, before he got the Manchester United job. They think the director of football doesn't have enough experience to be the director of football at a club as big as Manchester United.

"Then you've got INEOS and Jim Ratcliffe, who own around 30 per cent of the club, who are in charge of football operations. But everything has to be signed off by the Glazer family as well.

"Will it be a unanimous decision to part ways with Carrick if they finally do decide that he is going to be sacked? Will it be a unanimous decision that they get Mauricio Pochettino?

"I'm just intrigued to know who at Manchester United is really pushing for Pochettino to get the job. Is it the Glazer family? Is it Ratcliffe and Ineos? Is it Berrada and Wilcox? Do the Glazers see Mauricio Pochettino as the man to turn around United's fortunes?"

'Ratcliffe hasn't been very successful at sorting out the structure'

"Despite the fact that Jim Ratcliffe is in charge of football operations, the Glazer family own more shares than he does.

"So ultimately, if the club belongs to anybody, it still belongs to the Glazer family. And it's only natural that they would want a say in who is going to be the manager.

"Because from the US, they're watching this all unfold. They're seeing somebody who they sold 30 per cent of the club to, who basically said I want to take control of football operations. I can do a better job than the Glazers.

"They are watching him do a worse job than they were doing on the pitch. Because if they do fire Carrick and appoint Mauricio Pochettino, Pochettino will be the fourth manager they have had in three seasons. And that is under Jim Ratcliffe.

"And when Jim Ratcliffe came in, he said, one of the big problems at United has been that we've been hiring and firing too many managers. And it's not the manager's fault. It is something to do with the structure at the club.

"And that is something that he was going to sort out. Obviously, looking from the outside in, he hasn't done that so far."

articles.title: Man Utd manager: Mauricio Pochettino's decade-long courtship - but Michael Carrick deserves better
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino looks set to turn a decade-long courtship with Man Utd into a full-blown relationship, says chief football writer Phil McNulty.
articles.body:
When the expected formalities of Michael Carrick's dismissal as Manchester United are completed after a summit meeting in Monaco, Mauricio Pochettino looks set to turn a decade-long courtship with Old Trafford into a full-blown relationship.

Pochettino and United go back a long way, with the Argentine's name associated with the club since he was spotted leaving a lunch appointment at Scott's restaurant in Mayfair with Sir Alex Ferguson in 2016.

Ferguson was three years into his retirement, while Pochettino was building his reputation at Tottenham , where he fashioned an intense, all-out-attacking team that the great Scot admired.

Pochettino called it "a meeting in London between colleagues, between a genius and an apprentice".

Pochettino was mentioned as a contender to succeed Louis van Gaal when he was sacked by United in May 2016, then when Jose Mourinho suffered the same fate in December 2018.

Pochettino was the other name on United's shortlist when Erik ten Hag was appointed in April 2022, then again when the Dutchman was shown the door in October 2024.

Finally, as Carrick awaits what looks to be the inevitable, it looks like Pochettino will inherit the Old Trafford empire.

The problem for Pochettino is that the once great footballing empire is crumbling before the eyes, the dysfunctional product of years of poor decision-making and questionable appointments, allied to a Frankenstein's monster of a squad assembled by six managers.

One of Pochettino's quirks is to have a box of lemons in his office, believing they absorb negative energy. He will need several truckloads of the industrial strength variety to suck away the current mood at Old Trafford.

First things first, however, and that means waiting for the official confirmation of Carrick's departure, a long drawn-out affair which does little credit to part-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

Carrick, 45, has proved to be out of his depth since being confirmed as permanent head coach following a successful interim spell, but his history of success as a player, his basic decency and his obvious desire to turn United's fortunes around makes the ham-fisted handling of his sacking another uncomfortable episode.

It is an emotion reflected by United's increasingly disaffected fanbase, who have made it clear who they blame for their current place in the Premier League relegation zone.

Pochettino ready to accept Man Utd offer to replace Carrick

The Monaco summit that will decide the future of Carrick and Man Utd

Would Pochettino be the right appointment to replace Carrick? Have your say

Pochettino's appointment would land in the middle ground between the flawed sentimentalism of turning to fan favourites with little or no track record of success, such as Carrick and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, as well as the quick fix of bringing in proven past winners such as Van Gaal and Mourinho.

With his one-time dream of returning to Spurs now seemingly out of reach forever, Pochettino is ready to pick up the reins at the fallen giants that are United, another club he has clearly always had in his sights.

He is currently coach of the USA, whom he led at this summer's World Cup, but even then United were lurking on his agenda.

During the campaign Pochettino held court with invited journalists at the USA team hotel in California.

When mention was made of United, Pochettino turned to his closest confidante and ever-present assistant coach Jesus Perez to say: "One day, your dream comes true. You go to Manchester United ."

Perez replied with "United should have got you", promoting the response from a smiling Pochettino: "Future. Future."

The big question now is what Pochettino will United be getting?

He remains a beloved figure at Spurs , where he had an outstanding record of consistency following his appointment from Southampton in May 2014.

He never finished lower than fifth - in his first season - in any full campaign in charge, including second place behind Chelsea in 2016-17 and third in 2015-16 and 2017-18.

The one question mark always placed against Pochettino, including when he finished sixth at Chelsea in 2023-24, was an inability to get his teams over the line to tangible success in England.

Pochettino claimed the first trophies of his managerial career with Paris St-Germain after leaving Spurs - the 2021 French Cup and 2022 Ligue 1 title - but the club's hierarchy felt that was the minimum he should achieve given the squad at his disposal, and he did not see out his contract.

In England with Spurs , he was runner-up in the League Cup in 2014-15 and reached the FA Cup semi-finals in 2016-17 and 2017-18. In 2018-19 he reached the Champions League final and the League Cup semis.

In one season at Chelsea - a loveless relationship in which he could never shed his Spurs connections in the eyes of fans - he reached the FA Cup semi-finals and lost the League Cup final.

Pochettino's driven, competitive nature means that is an itch he will want to scratch when his United appointment is confirmed.

While Spurs have always appeared to be his first love, there is also no doubt United occupies a special place in his thoughts.

Spanish football expert Guillem Balague, who worked with Pochettino on his book Brave New World, says: "There is a fit with the people at the club too.

"Omar Berrada is a fan. When Manchester City drew up a shortlist to replace Pep Guardiola, some City supporters, including Omar, argued for Pochettino to be on it.

"There are plenty of clues about his feelings for United in the book. He was at the stadium in 1999 when United won the Champions League.

"Sir Alex Ferguson is mentioned 28 times, more than any other name in the biography.

" Spurs tried to push back and cut those references. Pochettino and I talked it over and decided that none of it would be touched. That shows how much it mattered to him."

Pochettino is a renowned builder, as he proved at Spurs after succeeding the sacked Tim Sherwood, working with Harry Kane to develop the recently crowned Ballon d'Or winner, as well as bringing Son Heung-Min to the club for a bargain £22m from Bayer Leverkusen in 2015.

If Pochettino can repeat that - a tough job in United's circumstances - and reproduce the easy-on-the-eye, attacking football played with relentless energy, then he could finally be the perfect fit Ratcliffe has so far looked in vain to discover.

Pochettino is also his own man, so it will be intriguing to see how he works with Ratcliffe, Berrada and Wilcox.

The road to Pochettino's sacking at Spurs effectively started following a friendly win against Real Madrid only weeks after their Champions League final defeat, when he made it clear he was not having enough influence at the club.

He enjoys warm relationships with his players, with a track record of improvement. It was no co-incidence that Cole Palmer enjoyed his best season working under Pochettino at Chelsea , scoring 25 goals in 45 appearances.

Pochettino, however, is also single-minded and ruthless, as he proved with an emphatic response to criticism for not phoning the players he left out of the USA World Cup squad.

He said: "When I was a player, when I didn't make the roster I didn't want my coach to call me. The players who didn't make the roster, they don't want to hear me say 'I apologise'. What are you going to say? Am I going to lie?"

He will need to call on every one of those qualities if and when he assumes control at United.

The final word on that day went to Pochettino as the pair argued over who was picking up the tab.

Ferguson said Pochettino could pay if he named an Argentina player who scored in the 1930 World Cup final.

Pochettino, in what he claimed was a moment of inspiration, named Guillermo Stabile.

He won that argument. Now both he and Ferguson will hope Pochettino can produce more moments of inspiration to win something more substantial at United.

articles.title: ¿Quién aguantará más?
articles.standfirst: Brahim, Balde, Rodrigo Mendoza o Endrick forman parte del grupo de jugadores de los tres primeros de la clasificación que no encuentra minutos
articles.summary: Brahim, Balde, Rodrigo Mendoza o Endrick forman parte del grupo de jugadores de los tres primeros de la clasificación que no encuentra minutos
articles.body: No hay sitio para todos. Es una canción habitual de todas las temporadas. Es lo que oyen en sus oídos futbolistas de renombre como Alejandro Balde, Brahim o Rodrigo Mendoza. Los planes de los entrenadores circulan por un lado y los sueños de los futbolistas, por otro. En esta campaña se suceden los casos de futbolistas de los tres primeros de la clasificación que se están quedando tras las cortinas. Los minutos pasan y el banquillo es una maldición. ¿Quién aguantará más en su situación? El caso de Alejandro Balde en el Barcelona es el del final de una seducción. Veloz, hábil y vertical, Balde parecía destinado a ser el dueño de la posición de lateral izquierdo en el cuadro azulgrana. De ahí a pasado a ser casi testimonial. Balde ha completado 100 minutos en esta temporada liguera. Lo llamativo es que el día que más jugó fue el del Clásico cuando entró en el césped durante una hora por la lesión de Espart. Su total es una cifra escueta que demuestra que no entra en el primer vistazo de Flick a la plantilla. La situación es más complicada si se revisan ambos laterales. En el derecho, con Koundé lesionado, la primera alternativa es Eric García y la segunda ha pasado a ser Fariñas. En el izquierdo, el de su especialidad, Balde está detrás del ahora dañado Espart y de Cancelo, que aprovecha su polivalencia para encontrar hueco en los dos perfiles. Si falla todo, aparece otro zurdo, Gerard Martín. Flick también le ha avisado de forma pública sobre su rendimiento. Balde aguantó el verano sin marcharse. Se aproxima el mercado de invierno. Uno de los jugadores que ha perdido relevancia en el Real Madrid es Brahim Díaz. El mediapunta suma 149 minutos en la Liga, una cifra alejada de los pronósticos iniciales de la temporada. Mourinho no ha encontrado en él un rendimiento que le haga dudar. Si se le quiere en el enganche Brahim lo tiene crudo con Bellingham y Güler. Si se le pone cerca de la banda tampoco mejora su porvenir. Brahim no está en el ostracismo ni Mourinho le tiene apartado en el garaje, pero si la temporada continúa así no sería extraño que hubiera noticias sobre su futuro. Menos minutos ha disputado Endrick, 84, que se encuentra en una situación similar a la de la temporada pasada, pero con una buena noticia que le protege: su espectacular rendimiento en varios episodios de la Champions. El brasileño, escorado a la derecha, fue clave en la remontada en Roma y agitó el partido en el reciente encuentro de Atenas. La temporada pasada se le abrió la opción del Lyon, excursión en la que su buena aportación le ganó ser llamado por Ancelotti para estar en el pasado Mundial. Muchos equipos estarán pendientes de la evolución del delantero en las próximas semanas. El pasado mercado de invierno se cerró con una operación rojiblanca estelar. El Atlético fichaba a Rodrigo Mendoza, centrocampista del Elche, tras un acuerdo de 16 millones de euros y unas cláusulas que podrían alcanzar otros cuatro 'kilos'. Medio fino, de gran calidad técnica, internacional sub-21, jugador de confianza para Eder Sarabia, no ha encontrado un hueco en la confianza de Simeone. Esta temporada luce 144 minutos, una minucia si se tiene en cuenta que por medio ha habido lesiones de Koke, Barrios o Cardoso. Mendoza aguarda el paso de las semanas para ver si mejoran sus perspectivas. Simeone parece más afín a perfiles diferentes al de un centrocampista que apuntaba alto hace sólo un año. Puede ser otra pieza codiciada en el mercado invernal. Las temporadas son tan volcánicas en los tres más grandes que el futuro es imprevisible, situación en la que ahora se ubican jugadores como Sorloth o Lookman, con un mercado inacabable. No sería insólito que al final el que pierda la paciencia sea algún futbolista inesperado.

articles.title: Las cuentas de España: puede ser primera este jueves ante la República Checa
articles.standfirst: Necesita que Inglaterra no gane en casa ante Croacia: si los de Tuchel vencen, habrá que esperar al Metropolitano para la resolución del grupo 3
articles.summary: Necesita que Inglaterra no gane en casa ante Croacia: si los de Tuchel vencen, habrá que esperar al Metropolitano para la resolución del grupo 3
articles.body: España se juega en las dos últimas jornadas ser primera de grupo en la UEFA Nations League antes de afrontar los cuartos de final como paso previo a la Final Four de junio. A España le vale con empatar ante Inglaterra aun perdiendo ante la República Checa este jueves, aunque hay un hipotético caso de que firme la primera plaza antes del partido del Metropolitano: si La Roja gana y no lo hace Inglaterra o si empata y pierden los de Tuchel. Todo lo que debes de saber sobre las cuentas del grupo 3 de la Liga A: ESPAÑA España ya se ha clasificado para los cuartos de final a falta de las dos jornadas. Se proclamará primera de grupo si vence a Chequia e Inglaterra no vence a Croacia, o si España empata e Inglaterra pierde. Si España pierde ante la República Checa, le vale el empate ante Inglaterra. En el caso de que lleguen empatados a puntos España e Inglaterra, se dilucidará el desempate de la siguiente manera: a. Mayor número de puntos obtenidos en los partidos de grupo disputados entre las selecciones en cuestión. b. Mejor diferencia de goles en los partidos de grupo disputados entre las selecciones en cuestión. c. Mayor número de goles marcados en los partidos de grupo disputados entre los combinados en cuestión; d. articles.title: Rocamora cita a 20 'Guerreras' para la recta final hacia el Europeo
articles.standfirst: El combinado nacional ya conoce a sus integrantes para el Torneo Internacional de España, que tendrá lugar del 27 al 29 de noviembre en Puertollano
articles.summary: La selección absoluta ya conoce a sus integrantes para el Torneo Internacional de España, que tendrá lugar del 27 al 29 de noviembre en Puertollano
articles.body: El seleccionador nacional, Joaquín Rocamora, ofreció la convocatoria de las 20 internacionales para afrontar el Torneo Internacional de España que se disputará en Puertollano y la última concentración de preparación antes del Europeo que se disputará en Polonia, Rumanía, República Checa, Eslovaquia y Turquía del 3 al 20 de diciembre de 2026. La lista combina la continuidad del grupo de trabajo de los últimos meses con la reincorporación de internacionales que han superado diferentes problemas físicos y que servirá para definir las 17 jugadoras que representarán a España en la cita continental. Entre las novedades destaca la presencia de la central Alicia Fernández, que regresa a la selección tras la lesión que arrastraba desde septiembre. Por su parte, Paula Arcos no podrá formar parte de esta lista por decisión médica, mientras que otras internacionales que no pudieron participar en los compromisos de octubre vuelven a estar disponibles. Las 20 convocadas se concentrarán el domingo 22 de noviembre en Madrid, desde donde viajarán a Puertollano para preparar y disputar el Torneo Internacional de España, que tendrá lugar del 27 al 29 de noviembre en el Pabellón Polideportivo Municipal Antonio Rivilla. España se enfrentará a Portugal, Argentina y Túnez en una última prueba antes de viajar a Turquía, donde comenzarán el Campeonato de Europa que se disputará del 3 al 20 de diciembre. Joaquín Rocamora destaca que el grupo amplio permitirá afrontar esta última concentración sin perder de vista el verdadero objetivo: llegar en las mejores condiciones al Campeonato de Europa. En este sentido, el seleccionador insiste en que “era importante el hecho de no perder el foco en ser mejores, el hecho de no perder el enfoque en prepararnos y el hecho de no perder el enfoque en que realmente lo importante es la semana siguiente en Turquía”. En cuanto a la composición de la lista, el seleccionador explica la ausencia de Paula Arcos, motivada por una decisión médica, y valora la incorporación de jugadoras que han dejado atrás diferentes problemas físicos, como Alicia Fernández. Sobre la situación del grupo, Rocamora reconoce que espera que no haya nuevas bajas por lesión: “Ojalá nosotros tengamos que tomar la decisión de descartar a las jugadoras, que no haya más jugadoras que se caigan por un tema de lesión”. De cara a la preparación en Puertollano, Rocamora explica que el cuerpo técnico ha preguntado a las propias jugadoras qué aspectos necesitan reforzar y en cuáles les gustaría sentirse más seguras. El objetivo será repasar las diferentes fases del juego, dar continuidad al establecimiento de roles iniciado en octubre y pulir los últimos detalles: “Le hemos pedido también información a las jugadoras, qué necesitan, en qué les gustaría sentirse más seguras y, a partir de ahí, hacer un repaso un poco de todas las fases del juego”. Por último, el técnico español recuerda que el modelo de juego continúa evolucionando, pero considera fundamental llegar al Europeo con confianza en las herramientas trabajadas: "El modelo de juego es algo vivo, es algo que se va a ir transformando a lo largo de todos estos meses, pero creo que sobre todo cuando se acerca la competición es importante que nosotras estemos confiadas en él”. articles.body:
Centre-back David Bates could win his first cap in seven years after being added to the Scotland squad for the matches against North Macedonia and Switzerland.

Bates, playing with Amedspor in Turkey, won the last of his four Scotland caps in 2019 and replaces fellow defender Luis Binks, who has withdrawn.

As well as spells in his homeland, 30-year-old Bates has club experience in Belgium, England and Germany, with most appearances coming at Mechelen.

He has started all 11 matches this season as Amedspor sit third in the Turkish Super Lig.

All of Bates' Scotland outings came under Alex McLeish while playing for Hamburg in the 2018-19 campaign.

Luke Graham, Jack Hendry and Ryan Porteous are the other central defenders in Sebastien Pocognoli's squad, though left-back Kieran Tierney can also operate in the head coach's preferred back three.

Brondby's Binks won his first three caps during Scotland's opening four Nations League fixtures, in which they picked up four points.

North Macedonia, who travel to Hampden on Friday, have no points in the section, with Slovenia three points better off than Scotland and Monday's hosts Switzerland on maximum points.

articles.title: Why is Pochettino the favourite to replace Carrick at Manchester United?
articles.summary: What would Mauricio Pochettino bring to the job if he replaces Michael Carrick in the Old Trafford hot seat?
articles.body:
If Michael Carrick’s departure as head coach of Manchester United is confirmed, Mauricio Pochettino is reportedly the man tasked with turning the fortunes of the Old Trafford club around.

United lie in the Premier League’s relegation zone, one point off the bottom in 18th, after winning just one of their opening 10 matches, that coming against Ipswich in August.

It’s the club’s worst start to a season in 30 years, and the expectations will be high for whoever takes the role, with their first league game coming away at bitter rivals Liverpool on November 22.

Pochettino – whose release from the contract extension he signed as USA head coach has reportedly been arranged while Carrick officially remains in position – would become the eighth permanent man in charge at Old Trafford since Sir Alex Ferguson’s departure in May 2013 after more than 26 years in the job.

The 54-year-old Argentinian was known during his playing career as a no-nonsense central defender, but as a manager he has evolved into one known for attractive, attacking football, with a focus on developing young talent.

He began playing in 1989 with Newell’s Old Boys before a switch to Spain in 1994, joining La Liga side Espanyol, where he played more than 200 league games across a seven-year career and broke into the Argentina squad, winning 20 caps and starting every game in the 2002 World Cup.

He had spells with Paris Saint-Germain and Bordeaux in France’s Ligue 1 before ending his career with Espanyol, for whom he passed 300 appearances in all competitions.

His first job in management came in January 2009, when he became Espanyol’s third coach of the season and successfully guided the Barcelona-based club away from the threat of relegation and beat city rivals Barcelona at Camp Nou for the first time in 27 years along the way.

He left the club by mutual consent in November 2012 and landed his first job in the Premier League at Southampton two months later, earning plaudits as Saints climbed the table before leading them to an eighth-placed finish in his first full season and the club’s highest points tally since the Premier League’s formation in 1992.

He moved to Tottenham in 2014 and oversaw the most successful run in the club’s recent history, reaching the League Cup final in his first season and finishing in fifth. He also allowed young prospects like Harry Kane, Dele Alli and Eric Dier the chance to shine – something which has been a focus for the Argentinian during his coaching career, often watching youth games and allowing young prospects to train with first-team set-ups to help their progress.

Spurs recorded their highest league finish since 1990 in 2016 and in 2017 finished second with a club-record 86 points, their highest finish since 1963.

Pochettino guided Tottenham to the Champions League final in 2019, overcoming Man City and Ajax in dramatic style along the way before losing 2-0 to Liverpool in the final in Madrid.

He was, however, sacked five months later after a poor start to the Premier League season before becoming head coach of Paris Saint-Germain from January 2021 to July 2022, departing after winning his first league title.

He spent the 2023-24 season in charge of Chelsea but departed two days after guiding the Blues to a sixth-place finish and took over the USA national team in September 2024, guiding the cohosts to the last-16 exit at the hands of Belgium at the 2026 World Cup before extending his contract in August.

Man United have long been associated with free-flowing attacking football, and Pochettino’s style was always likely to make him a more appealing option for the club’s hierarchy than the more pragmatic approach of another of the potential frontrunners for the job, Antonio Conte.

The Italian’s style is built more around tactical discipline, high work rate and defensive stability with reliance on quick counter-attacks.

Across his coaching career, Pochettino has become known for his attacking style of play, which relies on pressing high to win the ball back, focuses on keeping possession and usually adopts a 4-2-3-1 formation – which might suit the squad he inherits, as it becomes more of a 3-2-5 when building from the back, employing one inverted full-back and allowing the other to provide width in attack.

The likes of Bruno Fernandes, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo would likely thrive in his system, but the lack of a top-class No. 9 will be a hindrance, with Benjamin Sesko sidelined through injury and Joshua Zirkzee having struggled to make an impact.

The defence will come under huge scrutiny too; United have conceded 30 goals in their 15 games in all competitions this season and Pochettino’s defence can be exposed on the counterattack with so many men committed forward.

One of the factors which Pochettino is known for is his willingness to integrate young talent into training and match day squads and help establish a club’s identity, particularly at Southampton, where he previously worked with United’s Luke Shaw, and at Tottenham. That is also something United have traditionally been associated with, with Sir Alex Ferguson taking the likes of Ryan Giggs, David Beckham, Paul Scholes and Gary Neville and turning them into global stars. The likes of Shea Lacey might benefit particularly from Pochettino’s tutelage.

There might be some. One of Tottenham fans’ main gripes during Pochettino’s largely successful period at the club was that he prioritised league games over cup games, and team selections often reflected that.

United are already out of the League Cup, but a new boss appointed during the international break will face 16 games in 60 days starting with the trip to Anfield, with four Champions League games and an FA Cup third-round tie to fit in around 11 Premier League games which might prove crucial to their season.

Pochettino’s style also places a heavy reliance on fitness, intensity and discipline, something which has been somewhat lacking in large parts of the season so far at the Red Devils.

There were also issues arising from his spell at PSG. He was able to call upon some of the icons of the sport in Kylian Mbappe and Neymar in 2021, but PSG failed to win Ligue 1 for the first time in the past nine seasons, finishing a point behind Lille after losing four games down the stretch. He did win the title the following year, with Lionel Messi added to the ranks, but they failed to make even the quarterfinals of the Champions League or the Coupe de France.

articles.title: Manchester United reportedly closing in on deal with Mauricio Pochettino once team moves on from Michael Carrick
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino is expected to join Manchester United once Michael Carrick is out.
articles.body:
All indications point to USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino joining Manchester United, but there's one significant roadblock preventing the move: Michael Carrick is still employed by the side.

That's expected to change Wednesday, as Manchester United brass will reportedly meet to discuss Carrick's fate. Once that meeting takes place — and Carrick is relieved of his duties — it's expected Pochettino will be hired by the team , per multiple reports.

The move comes just months after Pochettino signed a new contract to continue coaching the USMNT through the 2030 World Cup. It will reportedly cost Manchester United $10 million to get Pochettino released from that contract.

With Manchester United facing relegation, the side is looking to make a significant move at head coach. Reports emerged Monday suggesting Carrick could be fired , with Pochettino among the biggest names Manchester United was considering as a replacement. Things have progressed quickly since then.

Pochettino would certainly qualify as a significant hire. The Argentine has extensive Premier League experience, having guided Southampton to its highest-ever finish in the competition and Tottenham to the 2019 Champions League final. He also managed Chelsea, with a stint at Paris Saint-Germain between his tenures at Tottenham and Chelsea.

After a year with Chelsea, Pochettino was hired to coach the USMNT, which he led to the Round of 16 at the 2026 World Cup.

The USMNT is currently preparing for the CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinals against Haiti. The team's are expected to play Saturday and Tuesday. It's unclear if Pochettino will be with the team for either game. It's also unclear who would replace Pochettino if he leaves and takes staff members with him to Manchester United.

USMNT players were aware of rumors suggesting Pochettino might leave the team, though attempted to downplay the news Tuesday.

With the situation still unresolved as of Wednesday morning, Carrick is expected to take training with the team before a decision is made about his future.

articles.title: Italy vs France: UEFA Nations League – preview, team news, predictions
articles.summary: Kylian Mbappe ‘under treatment’ as Group A1 leaders France travel to Italy for a game at the San Siro, Milan.
articles.body:
Who: Italy vs France What: UEFA Nations League, Group A1 Where: San Siro, Milan, Italy When: Thursday, November 12, at 8:45pm (19:45 GMT). How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up from 16:45 GMT ahead of our live text commentary stream

Italy host France for a heavyweight Nations League clash as they meet in the penultimate group stage game.

Under Roberto Mancini, who is back in his second stint in charge of the Azzurri, Italy lost their first group game 2-0 to Belgium but subsequently recorded thumping wins over Turkiye and got an impressive draw in Paris .

Italy, who travel to Belgium for their final group game on Sunday, sit second in the group – one point ahead of the Belgians but three adrift of France.

Zinedine Zidane, who took over as France coach from Didier Deschamps after the 2026 World Cup, led Les Bleus to a 1-0 win in Turkiye, and victories over Belgium home and away – including a 4-1 thrashing in Paris.

Zidane certainly has plenty of history with Italy as a player; he spent five seasons with Juventus and famously got a red card after headbutting Italy’s Marco Materazzi in the 2006 World Cup final.

France, who host Turkiye in their final group game on Sunday, can secure their quarterfinal spot with victory over Italy.

France captain Kylian Mbappe did not take part in team training on Wednesday and remained “under treatment” ahead of his country’s Nations League match against Italy, Les Bleus’ coaching staff said.

The French staff did not provide any further details regarding the 27-year-old’s physical condition.

The Real Madrid forward is back in the France squad for this camp after missing their last three matches through injury.

Mbappe scored the winning goal in Zidane’s first match as coach against Turkiye in September, but had to leave the pitch shortly afterwards due to pain in his left knee.

Mancini injects youth into the Italy setup

AC Milan forward Alphadjo Cisse earned his first Italy call-up after an impressive start to the season. The 20-year-old has scored seven goals in 12 games in his first season with Milan, including a hat-trick in the Europa League win over Red Bull Salzburg last month.

Cisse is one of four new faces among the 31 players selected by Italy coach Roberto Mancini. Parma midfielder Simone Lontani, 18, is included along with Como teenagers Mattia Liberali and Riccardo Cassano.

Liberali, 19, scored in Como’s record-equalling 9-1 win over Lens in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Cassano, 17, has yet to make his Como first-team debut. He and Lontani will train with the senior squad from Sunday before rejoining Italy’s under-18 and under-19 teams.

What happened in the last Italy vs France game?

Michael Olise scored a superb goal but France were held to a 1-1 draw by Italy on October 2, 2026 in Zinedine Zidane’s first home game since being appointed coach of Les Bleus.

Four days after coming off the bench to score a stunning solo effort to give France a 1-0 win in Belgium, Bayern Munich star Olise again showcased his spectacular talent by smashing a shot in off the crossbar from a free kick early in the second half.

However, Inter Milan defender Alessandro Bastoni equalised for Italy midway through the second half to prevent Zidane from making it three wins out of three in charge of his country.

Mancini: “In football, results change everything, but we still need to work, raise the bar and improve as a team; results are not enough.”

“I like that we are building a group of young players, along with some experienced ones who aren’t here now because they have issues. We played some good games and they are building a nice bond.”

Zidane: [on the death of Tenerife’s Jesus de Miguel after an on-pitch collision] “I’m saddened by what happened, deeply affected. It even gives me goosebumps, because you never want to see something like that on a football pitch.

“Above all, I feel sad for the family. I hope I never see anything like that again on a football pitch for the rest of my life.”

The Opta supercomputer has made France the favourites, with a win probability of 47.4 percent.

Italy were given a 28.3 percent chance of winning, while a draw was estimated at a 24.3 percent likelihood.

Roma defender Gianluca Mancini has withdrawn from the squad with a muscular injury, so Juventus’s Federico Gatti has been called up to replace him.

Italy are also missing Giovanni Di Lorenzo, Giacomo Raspadori and Moise Kean due to injuries.

William Saliba, Maghnes Akliouche, Ousmane Dembele, Manu Kone, Pierre Kalulu and Esteban Lepaul have all been ruled out with injuries.

However, Les Bleus will welcome back Real Madrid’s Ibrahima Konate and Aurelien Tchouameni, who missed out on the last round of games due to injuries. Dayot Upamecano returns from suspension to bolster the defence.

articles.title: Vini invita a un partido del Madrid a un niño de Sudán sin piernas
articles.standfirst: "Me gustaría que vinieras a un partido del Real Madrid y pasáramos el día juntos", reveló el brasileño
articles.summary: "Me gustaría que vinieras a un partido del Real Madrid y pasáramos el día juntos", reveló el brasileño
articles.body: Vinícius Júnior, futbolista del Real Madrid, ha invitado a un partido del conjunto blanco a un niño de Sudán que no tiene piernas como consecuencia de un ataque con drones, además de mandarle un vídeo de apoyo en el que le desea que pueda volver a jugar al fútbol. Zaher es un niño de trece años que perdió las piernas hace dos en el citado ataque y cuyo sueño es volver a jugar al fútbol de nuevo gracias a las prótesis que lleva. En un reportaje con la cadena británica BBC, Zaher contó que su futbolista favorito es Vinícius Júnior y que ojalá pudiera conocerlo algún día. A través del Real Madrid, la BBC se puso en contacto con el jugador y este respondió con un mensaje en vídeo. "Me han contado tu historia", comienza el brasileño. "Sé lo difíciles que han sido estos últimos meses para ti. Espero que puedas hacer un buen uso de tus prótesis y que puedas volver a jugar al fútbol y encontrar la felicidad, te lo mereces. Me gustaría que vinieras a un partido del Real Madrid y pasáramos el día juntos". "Decidle que le quiero, que su mensaje me ha alegrado mucho", respondió Zaher. Habibah, la madre de este niño, estaba con él cuando el ataque sucedió en 2024 en Khartoum, la capital de Sudán. "Le miré y estaba sangrando, había sangre por todos lados. Estaba destrozado. Me preguntaba que por qué les había dejado cortarle las piernas". Tras conocerse su historia y su deseo de volver a jugar al fútbol, Zaher y su madre se trasladaron a El Cairo, donde el niño se sometió a una operación y se le implantaron dichas prótesis. "Sacarle una sonrisa era casi imposible, pero ahora puedes ver que ríe y que tiene una gran confianza en sí mismo", apuntó Habibah.

articles.body:
England captain Kane will win his 126th cap for his country against Croatia in the Nations League at Wembley. The landmark moment comes just weeks after he was crowned the best player in the world.

But while the striker has ended his long wait for team glory with back-to-back Bundesliga titles at Bayern Munich, as well as a German Cup, he is now eager to kick on again and land the most prestigious prizes for club and country.

"To win a team trophy with England, a major trophy, is my biggest dream," he said in a press conference on Wednesday when asked what comes next for him. "That's always been my biggest dream, to win a European Championship or a World Cup, or both, hopefully, but I know how difficult that is. Extremely motivated to do that.

"Individual accolades are incredible and things I'm proud of but ultimately they're a consequence of trying to make the team better and trying to win something with the team.

"With Bayern Munich, it's trying to win the Champions League. There are many trophies I haven't won and that's what motivates me.

"I'm surrounded by great teams with both club and country so hopefully it's an exciting time ahead."

In recent years, Kane has been able to shake off his reputation as a top player who didn't succeed on the big stage. He hopes that in the second half of his career he will be able to completely change the narrative about his time in the game, having gone 10 full seasons in the first team at Tottenham without lifting silverware.

However, he also recognises the difficult defeats helped propel him into becoming the player he is today.

"It was tough in those moments when you feel you're performing well and putting up great numbers but not winning the team trophies which is ultimately what you're playing for," he said.

"My situation was quite unique in that sense, I don't know if there has been another player like that who hasn't won for so long.

"If anything, it made me even more hungry. Year after year, going into the season without having won one made me motivated to do that and pushed me to another level that I might not have reached if I'd won early in my career.

"Once I won the first trophy at Bayern, it was a weight off the shoulders in terms of a talking point in interviews and press conferences. It helped me relax and feel more free without thinking too much and having that extra pressure.

"I'm in a sweet spot of my career where I've won many trophies in the last couple of years and hopefully loads more to go. Hopefully by the end of my career, I'll have 20+ trophies and those first 10 years might not be spoken about as much.

"What I achieved in those 10 years years and here at Tottenham, getting to the Champions League final, it doesn't mean nothing - it was a incredible step the club took."

Tuchel: 'Unique' Kane will build on his records

Paying tribute to his captain, England boss Thomas Tuchel says he anticipates a "beautiful occasion" at Wembley on Thursday - but says Kane also has a job to do.

"It's always nice if things are proven in sports - he has his prizes and records, he will build on these records, score more goals and get more games," said Tuchel.

"He will start for us and as captain. It's a big occasion to present the Ballon d'Or trophy to our fans and have it embedded in the same day he gets his all-time record for 126 matches, it's a beautiful occasion.

"It's a match that matters a lot to us, it's not a friendly. It's on Harry to digest it as quickly as possible. There will be a lot of praise and emotions before kick-off then we need him in the best shape to win the match for us."

Tuchel praised Kane's "unique" skillset as what has set him apart from other players in the past year.

Asked if there is another striker who can do what Kane does, Tuchel said: "Maybe not at the moment. Everyone plays differently. On the very highest level, Lionel Messi developed a completely new style of No 9 at Barcelona and dropped everywhere.

"But he was more of a dribbler and accelerator from these spaces, Harry is more a passer and an accelerator through his passing range. Everyone is different. Harry is quite unique in the way he does it.

"It's not the only thing, he's also in and around the box and you still want the ball to drop to him if it's a one or two-touch finish. He's the one who is clinical and finish on the very highest level.

"That's why he got the biggest individual award in the game because he's a unique player at the moment."

articles.title: Bristol City: Head coach Michael Skubala to be given opportunity to improve form
articles.summary: Bristol City chief executive Charlie Boss says head coach Michael Skubala will be given more time to improve their results.
articles.body:
Bristol City will give under-pressure head coach Michael Skubala the chance to improve their results, particularly at home, says chief executive Charlie Boss.

The Robins have lost their past four Championship matches at Ashton Gate, culminating in last Saturday's 5-0 drubbing by Norwich City which left them in 17th place.

"The game against Norwich was a long way short of our standards and in the days that followed there have been a lot of tough and honest conversations around the building," said Boss in a video message on the club website. , external

"Earlier this week the board met and we agreed to give Michael Skubala the opportunity to turn around the home form."

Skubala led Lincoln City to the League One title last season before joining Bristol City on a three-year-deal in May.

However, a run of only two wins from their past 10 matches has led to supporters voicing their concerns.

"A lot of fans made their feelings known loud and clear at Ashton Gate on Saturday and I want them to know everybody shares their frustration from the owners, the board and the players," added Boss.

"Michael Skubala more than anyone knows we need to improve - we wouldn't have made this decision if we didn't believe that together we can get through this difficult period."

Bristol City's next Championship match is at second-placed Middlesbrough on Saturday, 21 November (15:00 GMT) before home games against Wrexham and Swansea sandwich a trip to West Bromwich Albion.

articles.title: Ronnie O'Sullivan loses 4-0 to Shaun Murphy at Champion of Champions

articles.body:
Seven-time world champion Ronnie O'Sullivan suffered a 4-0 defeat by Shaun Murphy at the Champion of Champions tournament in Leicester.

O'Sullivan, who has been struggling for form, was playing for the first time since losing to Ka Wai Cheung at the Northern Ireland Open last month.

The 50-year-old found himself 2-0 down against Murphy, who knocked in a 68 in the second frame.

Murphy made a 41 break to take the next frame before taking a tense fourth frame 61-42 to secure victory and a spot in the last eight.

He will play the winner of the other Group Three match between world champion Wu Yize and Chang Bingyu.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino: Man Utd strike agreement with Michael Carrick's potential successor
articles.summary: Manchester United powerbrokers set to make a final decision on Michael Carrick's future after Wednesday's Monaco summit; Mauricio Pochettino, who has a £7m release clause in the contract he signed with the USA after the World Cup, has been lined up as his replacement
articles.body:
Michael Carrick took training on Wednesday and officially remains United boss.

He is likely to be relieved of his duties before the end of the week, once Omar Berrada, the chief executive, and Jason Wilcox, the director of football, have returned from their meeting with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday.

Pochettino is then expected to be confirmed as Carrick's replacement sometime afterwards.

The former Chelsea and Tottenham manager is currently in charge of the USA national team and he could remain in charge for their games on Saturday and Wednesday - both against Haiti - unless an agreement with the US Soccer Federation can be reached to release him earlier.

Pochettino looks set to become United's eighth permanent boss since the retirement of Sir Alex Ferguson 13 years ago.

The £7m release clause in Pochettino's contract is not thought to be an issue for United.

Berrada and Wilcox met minority owner Ratcliffe at a pre-planned meeting in Monaco to review the club's start to the season.

Carrick was handed a stay of execution after United's 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth in the Premier League last month, but momentum is now gathering behind a change in the dugout.

United have held talks over appointing Pochettino on three separate occasions prior to this and came close to appointing him a few times, including in 2022 when they hired Erik ten Hag instead.

Ferguson has long admired Pochettino and often had long conversations with the former Spurs boss following his matches against United.

The pair were pictured at a Mayfair restaurant in May 2016 amid speculation about Pochettino, then Spurs head coach, taking over from Louis van Gaal at Old Trafford. United subsequently chose to appoint Jose Mourinho.

It is understood Pochettino loves his job with the USA but feels he cannot say no to United.

The 54-year-old is ready to return to the Premier League two years after he was sacked by Chelsea. Pochettino considers his time at Stamford Bridge as successful but ultimately feels it was not the right fit.

Liverpool (A) - Premier League - Sunday November 22, live on Sky Sports

Sporting (A) - Champions League - Wednesday November 25

Brentford (H) - Premier League - Saturday November 28

Newcastle (A) - Premier League - Wednesday December 2, live on Sky Sports

Coventry (H) - Premier League - Saturday December 5

RB Leipzig (H) - Champions League - Tuesday December 8

Mauricio Pochettino and Manchester United have a well-established history. One where paths might have crossed long before now, numerous times, but somehow never managed to converge.

Could it be that we are finally to bear witness to the culmination of this elaborate 10-year dance of incompatible circumstances?

The Old Trafford hierarchy have always admired Pochettino from afar. He was on their radar while at Tottenham and again when it was clear his time at Paris Saint-Germain was coming to an end. The Argentine was eventually lured back to the Premier League but instead returned to London, signing with Chelsea.

All along this journey of complicated courtship, United were at play. There have been many sliding-door moments. At the time news broke of Chelsea's interest in Pochettino in 2023, United, coached by Erik ten Hag, had just been ripped to shreds by Sevilla.

The morning after that defeat all the back pages focussed on another humiliating capitulation in Europe. 'What the El was that?' one read. Another lay into the inadequacies of Harry Maguire's performance. No doubt both headlines have been recycled since. At United, the more things change, the more they stay the same.

Miraculously, it took another 18 months for the button to be pushed on Ten Hag. Four managers of varying permanency followed. Until another chance, a decade on from the first, has revealed itself to pursue the one that got away. Is this finally right place, right time for Pochettino?

Poch, nice guy by all accounts. But nice at United means nothing. He'll get eaten alive and spat out. United need a tough bloke to get under the skin of these over paid under performing players.

I don't think any manager in the world will get that team fighting for the title without serious change in recruitment and change at the top we'll be in exactly the same situation in 6-12 months time.

Another great manager who's going to end up being in the same scenario! Just another manager with the same results! It's the board! Not manager!

Why bring Poch when the issue are players with high salaries? Currently players have more say at a club then coaches. Players decide who they want to play for you can't make everyone happy.

Poch is the Argentine Carrick. What's he going to do any different to Carrick? And Wilcox will be loving it knowing he wont have to buy any players and Poch will just use the youth players. Another circus show about to begin.

Poch is a very good manager, would be very happy with him at United. The fans saying he's not good enough need to stop living in the past. We no longer attract world class managers and let's be honest there's only about 5 left in football.

Right choice about 10 managers ago… which elite club would appoint him now?

articles.title: Josh King: The making of the rising star tipped to become one of world's best players after England call-up
articles.summary: Fulham's Josh King is in England's squad to face Croatia and Spain; Alvaro Arbeloa says he has 'everything' to become one of the world's best; Sky Sports finds out how he flourished in Fulham's academy, despite interest from Chelsea, and why he's destined for the very top
articles.body:
"One of the most outstanding things about Josh is that whenever the level went up, whenever there was a pressure game, he loved it," adds Turnbull. "He loved it when things got hard. He loved it when there was a little bit of extra pressure.

"He wanted it. He wanted to feel like the pressure was on him and the responsibility was on him to produce for the team. He enjoyed that. You always saw the best of Josh when the ante was up. I never once saw him not deliver in those circumstances.

"We would play tournaments in France, Spain and Portugal, against the giants of Europe, and afterwards the staff from each club would have to pick the best player they'd seen across the weekend. I remember Josh winning that accolade more than once."

King's temperament now forms part of his appeal to Thomas Tuchel, who called him up for England ahead of Cole Palmer and Phil Foden . "It's the attitude and the personality," he said last week. It all bodes well ahead of a possible debut against Croatia or Spain.

Tuchel sees a bright future for King, who has represented England at every level from U15 up. He has another champion in Alvaro Arbeloa. "He has everything to become one of the best players in the world," said the Fulham head coach after his call-up.

Turnbull nods in agreement at the mention of that Arbeloa comment. "Development is never a straight line, so you can never really predict. But I'd be lying if I said I didn't think he could play at the very highest level of the game when I was working with him."

His talent prompted interest from elsewhere.

"Chelsea were considered the best academy in the country at that time," says Turnbull. "They were generally able to bring in any player they wanted. We were aware of interest, but you never felt like it would materialise because Josh and his family never courted it."

Turnbull, who most recently worked as assistant to Kieran McKenna at Ipswich, talks up the role of King's parents, Michelle, a university lecturer, and Steve, a lawyer, in keeping him grounded. He mentions King's private education and his multi-sport background too.

"If all you have is football as a young player, it piles even more pressure on your shoulders than if your identity is bigger than that," he says. "And I think that's something his mum and dad have taken very deliberate steps to try to curate over time."

He describes King as having a "level of maturity that wasn't typical of boys his age" - and ability to match. "Interestingly, for someone who works so hard and is really open to learning, his game hasn't changed that much. It was pretty fully formed when I met him.

"The most obvious thing with Josh, and you're seeing it in the Premier League now, is the way he moves. The way he twists and changes direction is probably his standout attribute.

"His receiving skills are also elite. There's no debate over that. His ability to receive the ball in small spaces and be able to retain the ball and still go forwards and twist and shimmy and beat opponents is of top Premier League level, I would say."

King has been showing those qualities on a regular basis for Fulham since making his senior breakthrough under Marco Silva. It is a testament to his ability that he has played more Premier League minutes than any other teenager in the last two seasons.

As in his academy days, he has happily taken on added responsibility this season. King has more goal involvements than any other Fulham player and ranks highly in several other attacking areas, reflecting his importance to the side in the No 10 position.

His success is no surprise to Turnbull. But there is satisfaction at some of the parts of his game in which King continues to show improvement. "The two big areas we focused on in his development plan were his ball striking and his left side," he says.

Fulham carefully tailored his training programme. Turnbull describes taking King out of group sessions for focused shooting practice. The fruits of that work at youth level are now apparent in his ability to generate immense power with minimal backlift.

His goal against Chelsea, when he beat Robert Sanchez at his near post, was one example. Others include a spectacular volley from outside the box parried by Lukas Hornicek against Newcastle and a thunderous shot onto the post against Coventry.

King also has a knack for arriving in the right place at the right time. He ranks behind only Erling Haaland for touches in the opposition box in the Premier League this season.

"That was the same throughout his youth career," says Turnbull. "He gets into those positions so easily because of his intellect, his positioning and his movement. His ability to get into those positions is of a world-class level. He has a fantastic instinct for it."

The only frustration, if there is one, is that he hasn't scored more goals. "Probably, to take himself to the next level, he just needs to become more decisive when he gets into those positions because he is certainly arriving there enough," adds Turnbull.

His shooting continues to be an area of focus under Arbeloa. The Spaniard has used King almost exclusively in the No 10 position this season. But Tuchel has talked up the value of his versatility and Turnbull sees his future slightly further back.

"I think probably his best position will end up being as a No 8.

"So, not quite a No 10, not quite a six, but someone that goes box to box, who can contribute in the final third, but who can also contribute to build-up.

"Because one of his best attributes is undoubtedly his ability to take the ball in build-up. He's so hard to get the ball off, and his understanding of how to progress the game is of a very high level.

"You would want to be able to maximise that, but you wouldn't want to restrain him from arriving in the final third as well. I think he can do everything. In an ideal world, you would want him to be there for the build-up, then follow the game up the pitch."

The extent of King's potential is made more tantalising by the fact that, at 19, he still has room for physical development.

"He was always what we call in academy circles 'under-maturated', playing against a lot of kids who were physically stronger," says Turnbull. "There's a lot of research that points to that being a positive thing, if you're under-maturated and you still survive.

"And Josh didn't just survive, he thrived.

"I look at Josh and I still think he hasn't even got close to developing into the athlete that he will be. And that's a great thought, because he is performing so well in the Premier League already.

"I think there's a lot more to come from him."

articles.title: Uefa Nations League: Dara O'Shea 'proud' of how Republic of Ireland handled Israel games
articles.summary: Republic of Ireland defender Dara O'Shea is "proud" of how he and his team-mates came through a trying October international window.
articles.body:
Republic of Ireland defender Dara O'Shea said he is "proud" of how he and his team-mates came through a trying October international window.

During a four-game Nations League schedule, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side lost away to Kosovo and drew at home to Austria - who they are preparing to face in return fixtures - but it was two games against Israel which tested their resolve.

O'Shea stepped in as captain in the absence of injured skipper Nathan Collins and the 27-year-old acknowledged it "was a tough situation to be in" as they faced Israel in two games on neutral territory.

The first of those resulted in a 3-0 victory for the Irish in Hungary, a game that looked in doubt the previous day when training was delayed as players took a vote on whether to play - amid protests over the Israel-Gaza war - with goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu making himself unavailable for selection.

The sides drew 1-1 in the second meeting in Serbia and, while the saga proved a challenge for all within the Republic of Ireland squad, O'Shea - who missed the second game for personal reasons - paid tribute to his team-mates for the support he received as stand-in skipper.

"I think I was quite lucky, I am really proud to be part of the group, with some great people in it," said the Ipswich Town captain.

"Even the players playing now as well, they are great leaders themselves. I never felt I was fully alone in having to do anything

"There were always people around me. I always keep level-headed, I don't get too high with the highs or too low with the lows."

He added: "Of course it was a difficult time, it was a time that I had to learn stuff about myself, how I was going to react to things. But I think as a group we did excellently.

"It was a tough situation to be in, but we overcame it as best we could. And I am really proud of the group and the staff."

'Great to have Collins and Coleman back'

Collins is back to lead the team for Saturday's trip to face Austria in Linz and the final League B3 game at home to Kosovo on Tuesday (both 19:45 GMT).

Also part of the squad is Seamus Coleman, who has taken on a 'hybrid role' despite not being named in manager Hallgrimsson's official 24-man squad.

"It's great to have them [Collins and Coleman] back," O'Shea continued.

"It would have been great if they were there in the last camp as well, but we had some really good people in that last camp who were doing great things.

"Nathan's the captain, so it's always great to have him back in. Seamus' knowledge is so, so valuable to us. I think we are a stronger group when we have them two with us."

Coleman has been without a club since leaving Everton at the end of last season, following 17 years with the Toffees.

The 38-year-old defender recently said he is considering retirement but Republic of Ireland assistant coach John O'Shea is delighted to have the Donegal man around the squad.

"It's us helping Seamus and Seamus helping us," O'Shea said of Coleman's role on the training pitch.

"To see the impact he's having, the quality that remains in his ability and the driving and pushing he's doing for everyone in the group has been good to see. Not much has changed."

articles.title: Football: MP calls for heading in training to be legally restricted
articles.summary: An MP is calling for legal safeguards to limit repetitive heading in football training, amid growing concerns about the risk of brain injury.
articles.body:
An MP is calling for legal safeguards to limit repetitive heading in football training, amid growing concerns about the risk of brain injury.

Grahame Morris, the Labour MP for Easington, submitted a parliamentary motion on Tuesday urging the government to take action to reduce the number of times a player can head the ball in training.

The Early Day Motion (EDM) describes the need to protect players' brain health as a "significant public health and player welfare issue".

"The aim of this EDM is to raise awareness of the growing body of evidence linking repeated head impacts, particularly from heading a football, to an increased risk of neurodegenerative disease," Morris told BBC Sport.

The motion encourages the government "to take a more active role in prevention, education and player protection" Morris added.

Morris's motion supports a national petition submitted in September by the charity Head Safe Football, and calls on the government to take a number of actions:

Impose legal limits on repetitive heading in football training

Establish a cross-departmental task-force involving medical experts, players representatives, campaign groups and football authorities to develop "enforceable heading safeguards"

Recognise chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) as a public health concern

Create a national action plan to protect players' brain health

Improve education and awareness of the risks associated with heading, including in schools and through the PE national curriculum

EDMs are seen as a means for MPs to express their opinion on a subject and to canvass support for their views. No matter how many MPs sign up to an EDM there is no guarantee that it will be debated in Parliament.

Football does already have restrictions around heading.

The Football Association has phased out deliberate heading in grassroots football matches for children aged 11 and under.

It has also issued guidance recommending limits on heading during training of no more than 10 headers per week at amateur level.

In the professional game in England, clubs have been advised to limit players to 10 "high force" headers a week in training.

Scotland has gone further, banning heading in training on the day before and after matches in the professional game.

However, campaigners such as Dr Judith Gates, founder of Head Safe Football, believe that voluntary guidance is not enough.

"What we are finding is that coaches and parents don't know of the guidance, or the ban. Or they do not know why it exists," she told BBC Sport.

"There needs to be greater clarity and greater specific restrictions in order to protect players of today and tomorrow."

Dr Gates, whose husband the former Middlesbrough player Bill died with CTE, a degenerative brain disease associated with repeated head impacts, accepts that enforcing a legal limit would be challenging.

Prime Minister joins calls for compensation scheme

The calls for greater protection came as Prime Minister Andy Burnham called, in an interview with the Telegraph, , external on English football to formally recognise the game's dementia crisis and establish an "industrial injuries" compensation scheme for former players.

In a statement to BBC Sport, he said: "I've spoken to families affected by dementia and brain injury and heard what they have been through.

"Their determination to get this issue taken seriously has been extraordinary, and they should never have had to fight so hard to be heard."

Burnham's intervention follows inquests into the deaths of former England World Cup winner Nobby Stiles and Scotland defender Gordon McQueen, which found repetitive heading had contributed to their deaths.

The Professional Footballer's association (PFA) and the Premier League set up a brain health fund which has provided about £1m annually since 2023. However, campaigners say this is not enough to meet the costs of care.

The Football Association has not financially contributed to the fund, but said it continued to invest in research and had introduced guidance across professional and grassroots football.

"While the link between heading in football and long-term brain health remains the subject of ongoing scientific and medical research, we have consistently been at the forefront of efforts to help improve the safety of our game," an FA spokesperson said.
