articles.title: Barcelona prioritise January move for €20 million-rated teenage defender – report
articles.summary: According to Ferran Correas of SPORT, Barcelona have decided to go after the signing of FC Twente defender Ruud Nijstad in the upcoming January transfer wind...
articles.body:
According to Ferran Correas of SPORT , Barcelona have decided to go after the signing of FC Twente defender Ruud Nijstad in the upcoming January transfer window as a priority.

Director Deco and the Barcelona sporting department want to strengthen Hansi Flick's defensive options, and the 18-year-old Dutchman remains high on their list despite the financial obstacles involved.

Barcelona opted not to sign a new central defender in the summer despite letting go of Ronald Araujo and Alvaro Cortes.

However, the injuries to Andreas Christensen, Eric Garcia, and Jules Kounde exposed the lack of depth in the position, leaving Flick short on options.

Even though Christensen is back, Barcelona's position on signing a reinforcement has not changed, as the club continue to see Garcia and Kounde as primarily options in the right-back position.

Barcelona ready to go after Nijstad again. (Photo by Mateo Villalba Sanchez/Getty Images for DFB)

It leaves the manager with only Pau Cubarsi, Gerard Martin and an injury-prone Christensen as main options at the heart of the backline.

As such, Barcelona have made the decision to go after a new centre-back in January, with the preference being to sign someone with a long-term view rather than a stop-gap fix for only the second half of the season.

And, even though there have been links to several players such as Natan of Real Betis and Manchester United star Lisandro Martinez, Nijstad has emerged as the priority target for Barcelona .

The Blaugrana made contact to explore a move for the defender last summer, but nothing materialised as Nijstad, who also attracted interest from other major European clubs, opted to stay at Twente.

The 18-year-old defender has a contract with the Dutch club running until June 2029, and his performances have pushed his valuation upwards.

Deco does not want to spend €20 million on Nijstad. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)

As such, Twente are looking for a transfer fee of around €20 million for the teenage centre-back, a figure Barcelona are unwilling to meet.

The Blaugrana appreciate the youngster's profile and value his immense potential, but see the transfer fee being quoted as higher than what they intend to spend.

Moreover, there is also the difficulty of Financial Fair Play, as the Catalans only have a margin of around €3-4 million. While that may have improved following Raphinha's renewal, it still restricts the club's spending power.

As such, the future of Alejandro Balde, who is linked with a January exit, could play a key role in Barcelona's pursuit of Nijstad.

articles.title: Aston Villa confirm another star has extended contract
articles.summary: Ian Maatsen has penned a new contract at Aston Villa until 2032, and says he is keen to kick on under boss Unai Emery having already established himself as a...
articles.body:
Ian Maatsen has penned a new contract at Aston Villa until 2032, and says he is keen to kick on under boss Unai Emery having already established himself as a key player.

Maatsen extended his stay at Villa Park on Wednesday, having arrived at the club in the summer of 2024.

The left-back discussed his relationship with manager Unai Emery, and what made him keen to continue at Villa Park.

"First of all, the way the club is progressing, in a good way," he said.

"A big part of this way is the coach, the vision he sees in this club, and everyone around him, and also my teammates.

"I really enjoy it. He's really demanding, but he's a very good coach who really gets into the details.

"He wants to make sure everyone is on the same page with the same plan, and it works. It's a very good relationship.

"I feel at home here and I can develop here. It motivates me to bring this club to special things with them, and that's the reason I signed the contract."

Asked on his favourite memories in claret and blue so far, last season's Europa League final and subsequent trophy parade sticks out for Maatsen, who was proud to be able to help the Villa faithful create special memories.

The Netherlands international added: "On the pitch is probably the Europa League final. A big trophy for the club.

"We hadn't won [a trophy] in many years, so it was a good contribution for us as a team and a group, but also for the fans, for the club itself.

"The parade, to celebrate with the fans, the people in Birmingham, the local people, it was a very special day.

"It felt good. You see how big Birmingham is and we have a lot of Aston Villa fans. It's good for the city to celebrate with us, so it was an amazing day."

Confirmation of Maatsen's new deal comes after Victor Lindelof also extended his stay at the club .

articles.title: Skeptics of West Coast Big Ten schools have been proved wrong
articles.summary: A lot of experts felt the Big Ten West Coast schools were going to remain mediocre, but that hasn't happened in 2026
articles.body:
In 2024 and 2025, the Oregon Ducks did well in the Big Ten, but none of the other West Coast schools met expectations. USC, Washington and UCLA all struggled. This year, Washington is still down, but USC, Oregon, and especially UCLA are in the hunt for the College Football Playoff in mid-November.

College football writer and analyst Dan Wetzel pointed out that after November 7's games, the USC-UCLA-Oregon trio is 22-5 overall, 14-4 in Big Ten games. Meanwhile, the Ohio State-Michigan-Penn State trio is a combined 16-11 overall, 8-10 in Big Ten competition.

The widely-accepted view - not unanimous, but noticeably prevalent - among college football pundits was that the long-distance travel from the Pacific time zone to the Central and Eastern time zones would handicap the West Coast schools in the Big Ten. The view contained a certain amount of logic, and to be perfectly fair, USC has struggled a lot under Lincoln Riley when playing Big Ten road games in the Central and Eastern time zones. However, UCLA and Bob Chesney are unbeaten this year. Oregon just went to Columbus and thrashed Ohio State. The idea that the deck would regularly be stacked against the West Coast Big Ten schools didn't account for the possibility that the Midwestern and Eastern Big Ten schools could fall on hard times, primarily due to bad coaching.

Ohio State is a mess under Ryan Day. Michigan is a disaster under Kyle Whittingham. Penn State is struggling under Matt Campbell.

What commentators thought was a travel and logistics problem is really just a coaching issue. If the West Coast Big Ten schools are better coached than the Midwestern Big Ten schools, the travel and logistics are secondary.

Now let's see if Lincoln Riley can outcoach Curt Cignetti in Bloomington, Indiana, this Saturday.

articles.title: Kane says England appearance record a 'testament to dedication'
articles.summary: England captain Harry Kane said breaking the Three Lions' appearance record in Thursday's Nations League clash with Croatia will represent a "testament to al...
articles.body:
England captain Harry Kane said breaking the Three Lions' appearance record in Thursday's Nations League clash with Croatia will represent a "testament to all the dedication" that has gone into his career.

When Kane leads England out at Wembley to win his 126th cap, he will surpass the previous record held since 1990 by former goalkeeper Peter Shilton.

It will be the latest landmark in an incredible 12 months for the Bayern Munich striker, who in October became the first English player in 25 years to win the Ballon d'Or.

The 33-year-old Kane is also England's record scorer with 91 goals.

"It's definitely up there as the biggest (achievement)," Kane told reporters on Wednesday.

"I think it showcases consistency at the highest level. Testament to all the dedication, the time people don't see that keeps me fit and healthy. This is one of the biggest milestones in my career."

Since leaving Tottenham to join Bayern in 2023, Kane has taken his game to another level.

Aside from scoring 156 goals for the German club, he has also finally laid a ghost to rest in winning the first silverware of his career, including Bundesliga titles in 2025 and 2026.

However, England have not won a major tournament since winning the 1966 World Cup on home soil.

Kane suffered fresh frustration in July as he lost in a World Cup semi-final for the second time when Argentina came from behind to beat England.

Kane said he hoped there was enough left in his legs for another tilt at the World Cup in 2030.

"In terms of what's next, I don't like to put limits -- 100 goals (for England) is a milestone to reach as soon as possible," said Kane.

"We've done extremely well in tournaments, going into latter stages.

"I'm feeling really good and hopefully there will be many more years to see what I can achieve."

Other near-misses with Kane for England include two losses in European Championship finals, in 2021 on penalties to Italy and then in 2024 to Spain.

But he went on to win his first trophy with Bayern the following season.

Kane said, despite the perpetual disappointments, he kept believing one day his luck would change in terms of silverware.

"Obviously after any big loss, especially a final, you look into everything, you try and analyse it," he said.

"I don't think I ever doubted that it would come."

Tuchel, speaking earlier Wednesday, was coy when asked if Kane was England's greatest footballer.

"He's up there of course. It's now proven. It's always nice if things are proven in sports -- he has his prizes and records, he will build on these records, score more goals and get more games.

"Tomorrow he will start for us and as captain.

"It's a big occasion to present the Ballon d'Or trophy to our fans and have it embedded on the same day he gets his all-time record for 126 matches, it's a beautiful occasion."
